question: A licensed broker owns a firm with several employees who prepare and file entries throughout the week. The broker rarely visits the office and provides no meaningful training or review of the employees' filings. What broader duty does this pattern of conduct violate?

options.A: The duty to obtain a separate broker license for each employee who files entries for the firm
options.B: The duty to renew the firm's continuous bond at the start of every calendar year before filing continues
options.C: The duty to notify every client individually each time a new employee is hired at the firm office
options.D: The duty to exercise responsible supervision and control over the firm's customs business

question: A broker discovers that CBP liquidated a client's entry using a classification the broker believes was incorrect, which resulted in overpaid duty on the shipment. Within how many days of liquidation must the broker generally file a protest to challenge this decision?

options.A: 180 days from the date of liquidation of the entry
options.B: Sixty days from the date the merchandise was physically released
options.C: One full year from the date of liquidation of the entry
options.D: Thirty days from the date the entry was originally filed with CBP

question: A broker is preparing to file an entry for goods that qualify as originating merchandise under the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement. How does this preferential origin status generally affect the merchandise processing fee that will be owed on the entry in this case?

options.A: It doubles the applicable ad valorem MPF rate on the entered value
options.B: It has no effect on the MPF calculation for this particular entry
options.C: It converts the MPF into a flat informal entry fee no matter the entered value
options.D: Qualifying USMCA-originating goods are generally exempt from the MPF

question: A client asks a broker to backdate a commercial invoice so that a shipment appears to qualify for an expiring preferential duty rate that it does not actually meet. What should the broker do in response to this request from the client?

options.A: Backdate the invoice, but keep an internal note recording that the request came from the client
options.B: Backdate the invoice, since the broker is only following the written instructions given by the client
options.C: Refuse the request, since certifying a fraudulent document violates the broker's integrity duty
options.D: Backdate the invoice only if the client first provides a signed written indemnification agreement here

question: CBP publishes an informed compliance notice announcing a significant change in how a category of merchandise should be classified. A broker who regularly files entries for that category never reviews the notice. What professional duty has the broker most clearly neglected?

options.A: The duty to stay reasonably current on CBP guidance affecting the broker's practice
options.B: The duty to notify every client individually within twenty-four hours of publication
options.C: The duty to immediately amend every prior entry filed under the old classification
options.D: The duty to obtain a new broker license reflecting the updated guidance

question: A broker is uncertain how a newly designed product should be classified under the HTSUS and the classification is not clearly resolved by existing rulings. As part of exercising reasonable care, what is an appropriate step for the broker to take before filing?

options.A: Ask the freight forwarder to select the classification on the broker's behalf
options.B: Simply pick whichever classification carries the lowest available duty rate
options.C: Request a binding ruling from CBP to resolve the classification with certainty
options.D: File the entry using no classification code until the matter is later resolved

question: A broker files an entry for merchandise released under immediate delivery procedures and now must decide how quickly the paperwork is due. Under standard CBP timing requirements, within how many working days after entry must the broker generally file the corresponding entry summary?

options.A: Thirty calendar days after the merchandise physically arrives at destination
options.B: Ninety working days after entry, an extended deadline reserved for bonded warehouses
options.C: Five working days after entry, a shorter deadline that does not generally apply
options.D: Ten working days after entry, which is the standard entry summary deadline

question: A broker is reviewing a printed CBP Form 7501 and wants to locate the entry's final combined charges before sending payment instructions to the client. Which figure on the form represents this combined total of duty, fees, and other assessed charges?

options.A: The summary line totaling duty, MPF, HMF, and any other assessed charges
options.B: The line showing only the entered value declared for the imported merchandise
options.C: The line showing only the calculated duty rate percentage applied to the entry
options.D: The line showing only the bond number referenced for this particular entry

question: A broker discovers that imported merchandise arriving from overseas lacks any country of origin marking on the goods themselves or their containers. Under 19 U.S.C. 1304, what is the most likely consequence for the importer if this is not corrected?

options.A: CBP will automatically waive the marking requirement for first-time importers of goods
options.B: The classification of the merchandise will automatically change to duty-free at entry
options.C: The goods may be subject to a marking duty or other penalty for noncompliance
options.D: The importer will receive an automatic extension on the entry filing deadline

question: A licensed customs broker has not filed a required periodic status report with CBP confirming the broker remains actively engaged in customs business. Under the customs broker regulations, what is this report generally called and how often is it due?

options.A: The continuous bond renewal notice, due whenever the bond amount changes
options.B: The triennial status report, due once every three years
options.C: The annual compliance certification, due once every year for the broker
options.D: The initial licensing application, due only once at the start of a broker's career

question: An importer emails a broker the HTSUS number it wants used on an upcoming entry, but the broker's own research suggests a different classification may better describe the merchandise. Under the broker's duty of reasonable care, what should the broker do before filing?

options.A: Independently verify the classification rather than simply filing the importer's number as given
options.B: File the importer's number exactly as the importer instructed without independent review before filing
options.C: Ask a competing broker informally which classification they would personally use for the same goods
options.D: Refuse to file the entry until CBP issues a binding classification ruling for the imported merchandise

question: After an entry has already been filed and liquidated, a broker discovers that the importer's prior entries understated the correct dutiable value for several years due to an internal accounting error. What is the appropriate next step for the broker to recommend?

options.A: Wait silently to see whether CBP ever discovers the error independently at audit
options.B: File a prior disclosure with CBP to voluntarily correct the understatement
options.C: Simply correct the value going forward without addressing the earlier entries
options.D: Advise the importer to stop importing the goods to avoid any further liability

question: Riverside Paper Company, a New Orleans importer, enters coated paper rolls with an entered value of $70,000 and a duty rate of 4%. Assume a 0.3464% ad valorem MPF within the statutory range and a 0.125% ad valorem HMF. What is the total amount of duty plus fees owed on this entry?

options.A: $3,129.98, combining duty, MPF, and HMF together fully
options.B: $2,887.50, covering duty and HMF alone on this shipment
options.C: $3,829.98, applying a five percent duty rate instead
options.D: $3,042.48, covering duty and MPF alone on this shipment

question: Bluewater Seafood, a Boston importer, files an ocean entry for frozen shrimp with an entered value of $55,000 and a duty rate of 5%. Assume a 0.3464% ad valorem MPF within the statutory range and a 0.125% ad valorem HMF. What is the total amount of duty plus fees owed on this entry?

options.A: $2,818.75, covering duty and HMF alone on this shipment
options.B: $3,009.27, combining duty, MPF, and HMF together fully
options.C: $3,559.27, applying a six percent duty rate instead
options.D: $2,940.52, covering duty and MPF alone on this shipment

question: A broker's former employee, now working for a competing firm, asks the broker to share a mutual client's shipment history to help the new firm prepare a competitive bid. The client has not consented to this disclosure. What must the broker do?

options.A: Share only the shipment volumes, since dollar figures are the more sensitive commercial detail here
options.B: Share the information informally, since the two brokers previously worked together at the same firm
options.C: Decline the request, since client information may not be disclosed without the client's consent
options.D: Ask the former employee to sign a confidentiality agreement before sharing any of the client data

question: Atlas Hardwood Company, a Charleston importer, enters maple flooring with an entered value of $27,500 and a duty rate of 5.5%. Assume a 0.3464% ad valorem MPF within the statutory range and a 0.125% ad valorem HMF. What is the total amount of duty plus fees owed on this entry?

options.A: $1,642.14, combining duty, MPF, and HMF together fully
options.B: $1,546.88, covering duty and HMF alone on this shipment
options.C: $1,917.14, applying a six and a half percent duty rate
options.D: $1,607.76, covering duty and MPF alone on this shipment

question: Titan Industrial Supply, a Houston importer, enters stainless fasteners with an entered value of $100,000 and a duty rate of 4%. Assume a 0.3464% ad valorem MPF within the statutory range and a 0.125% ad valorem HMF. What is the total amount of duty plus fees owed on this entry?

options.A: $4,125.00, covering duty and HMF alone on this shipment
options.B: $4,346.40, covering duty and MPF alone on this shipment
options.C: $5,471.40, applying a five percent duty rate instead
options.D: $4,471.40, combining duty, MPF, and HMF together fully

question: Skyline Pharma Logistics, a Memphis air broker, files an air entry for vaccines with an entered value of $22,000 and a duty rate of 2.5%. Assume a 0.3464% ad valorem MPF within the statutory range, and remember that air shipments carry no harbor maintenance fee. What is the total duty plus MPF owed on this entry?

options.A: $550.00, representing the calculated duty amount by itself
options.B: $653.71, mistakenly including a harbor maintenance fee amount
options.C: $626.21, combining the duty amount with the calculated MPF
options.D: $736.21, applying an incorrect three percent duty rate

question: A formal entry covering a modest shipment of hand tools has an entered value of $9,000. Assume a 0.3464% ad valorem MPF subject to a $32.71 statutory minimum. What MPF amount should the broker actually enter on the 7501 for this shipment?

options.A: $32.71, the statutory minimum applied to this entered value
options.B: $31.18, the uncapped ad valorem calculation rounded to cents
options.C: $9.00, mistakenly treating the entered value itself as the fee
options.D: $34.64, an unrelated figure not derived from this entered value

question: Cornerstone Crafts, a Portland importer, enters handmade ceramics with an entered value of $6,500 and a duty rate of 3%. Assume a 0.3464% ad valorem MPF subject to a $32.71 statutory minimum, and a 0.125% ad valorem HMF. What is the total amount of duty plus fees owed on this entry?

options.A: $227.71, covering duty and minimum MPF alone here
options.B: $203.13, covering duty and HMF alone on this shipment
options.C: $225.65, using the uncapped MPF figure instead of the minimum
options.D: $235.84, applying the statutory minimum MPF of $32.71

question: A broker is training an assistant on the merchandise processing fee and wants to explain the point at which the statutory maximum begins to apply. Assuming an ad valorem MPF rate of 0.3464% and a statutory maximum MPF of $634.62, approximately what entered value must a formal ocean entry reach before the calculated MPF first hits that maximum cap?

options.A: Approximately $150,000, well below where the cap is actually reached
options.B: Approximately $183,225, the point where the cap is first reached
options.C: $634.62, mistakenly treating the fee cap as an entered value
options.D: Approximately $200,000, somewhat above where the cap is actually reached

question: A single truck entry has two line items: entered value $12,000 with a 5% duty rate, and entered value $8,000 with an 8% duty rate. Assume a 0.3464% ad valorem MPF on the combined $20,000 entered value and no HMF since this is a truck shipment. What is the total amount owed?

options.A: $1,309.28, combining the total duty with the calculated MPF
options.B: $1,240.00, representing the combined duty amount on both line items by itself
options.C: $1,429.28, swapping the duty rates between the two line items on the entry
options.D: $69.28, representing the calculated MPF amount on the combined entered value

question: Evergreen Beverage Partners, a Seattle importer, files an ocean entry for sparkling mineral water with an entered value of $120,000 and a duty rate of 1.5%. Assume a 0.3464% ad valorem MPF within the statutory range and a 0.125% ad valorem HMF. What is the total amount of duty plus fees owed on this entry?

options.A: $2,965.68, applying a two percent duty rate instead
options.B: $1,950.00, covering duty and HMF alone on this shipment
options.C: $2,365.68, combining duty, MPF, and HMF together fully
options.D: $2,215.68, covering duty and MPF alone on this shipment

question: Brightpath Tooling, a Houston importer, enters hand tools subject to an antidumping order, with an entered value of $40,000, a regular duty rate of 3%, and an additional antidumping duty rate of 25% of entered value. Assume a 0.3464% ad valorem MPF within range and a 0.125% ad valorem HMF. What total amount is owed including the antidumping duty?

options.A: $11,200.00, mistakenly omitting the MPF and HMF amounts from the total
options.B: $11,388.56, combining regular duty, antidumping duty, MPF, and HMF
options.C: $9,388.56, calculating the antidumping duty at 20% instead of 25%
options.D: $1,388.56, mistakenly omitting the antidumping duty from the total

question: Gulf Coast Marine Supply, a Tampa importer, files an ocean entry for boat anchors with an entered value of $33,000 and a duty rate of 7%. Assume a 0.3464% ad valorem MPF within the statutory range and a 0.125% ad valorem HMF. What is the total amount of duty plus fees owed on this entry?

options.A: $2,424.31, covering duty and MPF alone on this shipment
options.B: $2,351.25, covering duty and HMF alone on this shipment
options.C: $2,465.56, combining duty, MPF, and HMF together fully
options.D: $2,795.56, applying an eight percent duty rate instead

question: Summit Appliance Corporation, a Los Angeles importer, enters refrigerators with an entered value of $600,000 and a duty rate of 2%. Assume a 0.3464% ad valorem MPF capped at $634.62 and a 0.125% ad valorem HMF with no cap. What is the total amount of duty plus fees owed on this entry?

options.A: $12,750.00, covering duty and HMF alone on this entry
options.B: $12,634.62, covering duty and capped MPF alone here
options.C: $14,828.40, using the uncapped MPF figure instead of the cap
options.D: $13,384.62, applying the statutory MPF cap of $634.62

question: A broker is checking the fee section of a formal consumption entry for imported garden tools with an entered value of eighty-eight thousand dollars. For this exercise only, assume an ad valorem MPF rate of 0.3464 percent, a statutory minimum of $32.71, and a statutory maximum of $634.62. What MPF amount should be reported?

options.A: $304.83, the calculated amount that falls between the minimum and maximum
options.B: $634.62, the statutory maximum applied in place of the calculated amount at entry
options.C: $32.71, the statutory minimum applied in place of the calculated amount here
options.D: $3,048.30, the calculated amount with the decimal point moved one place over

question: An informal mail entry has an entered value of $1,500 and a duty rate of 2.5%. Assume the informal entry MPF flat fee is $2.18 and that mail shipments carry no harbor maintenance fee. What total amount of duty plus MPF is owed?

options.A: $37.50, representing the calculated duty amount by itself
options.B: $41.68, mistakenly adding the flat fee twice over
options.C: $35.32, mistakenly subtracting the flat fee from duty
options.D: $39.68, combining the duty amount with the flat MPF

question: Rockford Furniture Group, a Savannah importer, files an ocean entry for oak chairs with an entered value of $90,000 and a duty rate of 3.5%. Assume a 0.3464% ad valorem MPF within the statutory range and a 0.125% ad valorem HMF. What is the total amount of duty plus fees owed on this entry?

options.A: $3,461.76, covering duty and MPF alone on this shipment
options.B: $3,262.50, covering duty and HMF alone on this shipment
options.C: $3,574.26, combining duty, MPF, and HMF together fully
options.D: $4,024.26, applying a four percent duty rate instead

question: An ocean vessel delivers a consolidated shipment with two line items. The first line has an entered value of fifteen thousand dollars at six percent duty, and the second has an entered value of twenty-five thousand dollars at two percent duty. Assume a 0.3464 percent ad valorem MPF within range and a 0.125 percent HMF. What total is owed?

options.A: $1,588.56, the duty, the merchandise processing fee, and the harbor fee combined
options.B: $1,450.00, the duty plus the harbor maintenance fee on the combined entered value
options.C: $1,538.56, the duty plus the merchandise processing fee on the combined entered value
options.D: $1,400.00, the combined duty on the two line items by itself without fees added

question: A broker is preparing an ocean entry for a shipment of consumer electronics with an entered value of $500,000. Assume a 0.3464% ad valorem MPF subject to a $634.62 statutory maximum cap. What MPF amount should the broker enter on the 7501 for this shipment?

options.A: $1,732.00, the full uncapped ad valorem MPF calculation
options.B: $634.62, the statutory maximum cap applied to this shipment
options.C: $634.16, a slightly misremembered version of the statutory cap
options.D: $32.71, confusing the statutory minimum with this shipment's fee

question: A broker files an ocean entry with an entered value of $50,000 and a duty rate of 5%. Assume a 0.3464% ad valorem MPF and a 0.125% ad valorem HMF, with the MPF falling between the statutory minimum and maximum. What total amount of duty plus fees is owed on this entry?

options.A: $2,562.50, covering duty and HMF only for this shipment
options.B: $2,673.20, covering duty and MPF only for this shipment
options.C: $2,908.90, using a six percent duty rate calculation instead
options.D: $2,735.70, covering duty, MPF, and HMF combined together

question: A new employee at a brokerage computes the merchandise processing fee on an amount that already includes the harbor maintenance fee, then adds the two charges together for an ocean entry. According to the chapter, how should each fee be computed when arriving at the total amount due?

options.A: Each fee is computed independently against entered value or cargo value
options.B: Each fee is computed on the running total after the previous fee is added
options.C: Each fee is computed on the total amount due at the bottom of the form
options.D: Each fee is computed on the duty amount rather than on the merchandise value

question: A formal ocean entry covers imported rugs with an entered value of nine hundred thousand dollars. For this exercise only, assume a 0.3464 percent ad valorem MPF with a $634.62 statutory maximum and a 0.125 percent harbor maintenance fee. What combined fee amount, excluding duty, should the broker report?

options.A: $4,242.60, the uncapped processing fee plus the harbor maintenance fee amount
options.B: $1,125.00, the harbor maintenance fee amount reported by itself on the entry
options.C: $634.62, the capped processing fee amount reported by itself on the entry
options.D: $1,759.62, the capped processing fee plus the harbor maintenance fee amount

question: A shipment of imported copper wire with a quantity of one thousand two hundred fifty kilograms and an entered value of forty-eight thousand dollars carries a rate of four and one half percent of value plus eighty-six cents per kilogram. What amount should the broker enter as duty in column 35 for this line?

options.A: $2,160.00, the ad valorem portion of the compound rate applied to the value
options.B: $3,235.00, the ad valorem and specific portions of the compound rate combined
options.C: $1,075.00, the specific portion of the compound rate applied to the quantity
options.D: $5,910.00, the ad valorem portion plus the specific portion counted twice over

question: A broker is reviewing an HTSUS provision that imposes a duty of six percent of value plus twenty-five cents for each kilogram of imported merchandise. The broker must record this rate on the line-item area of the entry summary. Which of the following best describes how such a rate appears in column 34?

options.A: A compound rate combining an ad valorem percentage and a specific amount per unit
options.B: A specific rate stated only as a dollar figure for each unit of measure imported at entry
options.C: An ad valorem rate stated only as a percentage of the entered value declared here
options.D: A flat fee amount charged for processing the entry rather than a duty rate

question: An ocean vessel unloads imported hardwood flooring at a US seaport with a cargo value of two hundred forty thousand dollars. For this exercise only, assume a harbor maintenance fee rate of 0.125 percent of cargo value. What HMF amount should the broker report for this entry?

options.A: $240.00, a fee computed by applying a rate of one tenth of one percent
options.B: $300.00, the fee computed as a percentage of the cargo value
options.C: $3,000.00, a fee computed by applying a rate of one and one quarter percent
options.D: $0.00, because harbor maintenance fees are capped at a stated ceiling amount

question: An importer asks a broker to explain which figure on the entry summary becomes the basis for the ad valorem duty that CBP will assess on a shipment of imported leather belts. Which column of CBP Form 7501 reports the value the importer declares as the basis for duty?

options.A: Column 33, which reports the entered value declared for the line item
options.B: Column 32, which reports the net quantity in the HTSUS units for the line
options.C: Column 34, which reports the rate of duty applicable to the line item
options.D: Column 35, which reports the duty and internal revenue tax amount owed

question: During a review of a completed entry summary for imported ceramic vases, a broker finds that the ten-digit HTSUS number in column 29 was entered for a different product. What is the effect of this kind of classification error on the rest of the entry?

options.A: The error changes only the description in column 28 without affecting any amount
options.B: The error changes the entered value in column 33 but leaves the duty rate in place
options.C: The error changes the gross weight in column 30 but no other figure on the form
options.D: The error changes the rate in column 34, the duty in column 35, and the total due

question: A broker is assembling the total amount due on an ocean entry for imported aluminum extrusions that also carries an antidumping duty deposit and a federal excise charge. Where do these additional charges fit into the calculation described in the chapter?

options.A: They replace the harbor maintenance fee on entries subject to a deposit
options.B: They are added to entered value before the duty rate is applied
options.C: They are added after duty, merchandise processing fee, and harbor fee
options.D: They are subtracted from the duty before the total amount is computed

question: Before calculating the merchandise processing fee on an entry for merchandise that may qualify for preferential treatment under a trade agreement, a broker should complete a specific step. According to the chapter, what must the broker confirm before computing the fee?

options.A: Whether an exemption from the fee applies to the merchandise being entered
options.B: Whether the importer prefers to pay the fee later with the duty deposit
options.C: Whether the shipment qualifies for a reduced duty rate before filing
options.D: Whether the freight forwarder has already paid the fee on the client's behalf

question: A rail shipment from Mexico carries a value of eighteen thousand dollars, and the importer also supplied free molds valued at six thousand dollars that were used solely to make this shipment's goods. Assume a five percent duty rate and a 0.3464 percent ad valorem MPF within the statutory range. What total duty and MPF is owed?

options.A: $900.00, the five percent duty computed on the invoice value of the goods alone
options.B: $1,200.00, the five percent duty computed on the value including the molds only
options.C: $1,283.14, the duty and processing fee computed on the value including the molds
options.D: $962.35, the duty and processing fee computed on the invoice value alone for this entry

question: A broker is reviewing the lower portion of an entry summary for an ocean shipment of imported furniture that also carries an antidumping duty order. Which items belong in the summary block of other charges below the line items on CBP Form 7501?

options.A: The classification number, the rate of duty, and the entered value declared for each line item
options.B: The merchandise processing fee, the harbor maintenance fee, and the antidumping deposit
options.C: The gross weight, the manifest quantity, and the net quantity reported for each line item
options.D: The importer of record number, the consignee number, and the port of entry identification code

question: A client supplies a broker with a classification the client insists is correct, but the broker's own review of the HTSUS shows a different heading clearly applies, and the client's heading carries a much lower rate. The broker must decide how to proceed. What does the duty of reasonable care require?

options.A: The broker must use the correct classification and not file the lower-rate heading
options.B: The broker must follow the client's heading because the client provided the information
options.C: The broker must file the client's heading and note the disagreement in the file
options.D: The broker must withdraw from all future work for this client immediately

question: An importer supplies a foreign manufacturer with a free die valued at thirty thousand dollars that will be used to produce the current order and two later orders of imported metal brackets. The broker is preparing the entry for the first order. How should the die's value be treated in entered value for this shipment?

options.A: The full die value is added because the die is a buyer-supplied assist
options.B: A reasonable portion of the die value is allocated and added for this entry
options.C: The die value is excluded because the importer did not pay the manufacturer for it
options.D: The die value is excluded because tools used abroad are not part of entered value

question: A broker is explaining the line-item fields on CBP Form 7501 to a new employee who has asked about the two weight and quantity columns that sit between the classification number and the entered value. What do columns 30 and 31 of the form report?

options.A: The net quantity in HTSUS units and the entered value declared for duty purposes
options.B: The rate of duty and the resulting duty amount computed on the line
options.C: The importer of record number and the consignee identification number at entry
options.D: The gross weight and the manifest quantity, used for statistical reporting

question: A trainee preparing a first entry summary asks the broker which part of the work should come first when a fact pattern gives a description of merchandise, an invoice price, and a duty rate. According to the chapter, what order should the trainee follow?

options.A: Determine the fees first, then classify, then value, then compute the duty owed on the entry
options.B: Classify the merchandise first, then determine value, then multiply, then add fees
options.C: Compute the duty first, then value the goods, then classify, then add the fees due
options.D: Value the merchandise first, then classify, then add fees, then multiply them together

question: A manufacturer uses only imported industrial sewing machines as components in packaging lines that are exported to Brazil and cannot trace individual machines to specific exports. The manufacturer wants substitution manufacturing drawback. Which requirement of section 1313(b) is missing from these facts?

options.A: The manufacturer must also use domestic or other merchandise of the same kind and quality.
options.B: The manufacturer must export twice as many finished articles as it imports machines into the country
options.C: The manufacturer must obtain a textile visa for each imported industrial machine at the port
options.D: The manufacturer must destroy the machines rather than export or sell them abroad

question: A new broker asks a mentor why customs brokers carry such extensive ethical obligations, since the broker's role is to help importers move goods quickly through the entry process. The mentor explains the source of those obligations. Which statement best describes the broker's position?

options.A: The broker acts solely as an advocate for the importer in all matters
options.B: The broker acts solely as an enforcement officer for the federal government
options.C: The broker holds a position of trust between importers and the government
options.D: The broker's obligations arise only from the terms of the client contract

question: A broker is comparing the merchandise processing fee with the harbor maintenance fee for the same ocean entry and wants to explain the difference in how the two fees respond to very large values. Which statement correctly describes HMF on a standard import entry as compared with the ad valorem MPF?

options.A: HMF is subject to the same floor and ceiling amounts that apply to the ad valorem MPF
options.B: HMF stops accruing once it reaches one half of the MPF ceiling amount
options.C: HMF carries a per-entry ceiling but no corresponding floor amount on the entry
options.D: HMF is computed as a straight percentage with no per-entry floor or ceiling

question: An air shipment of imported steel fasteners has an entered value of twenty-six thousand dollars and an ordinary duty rate of two percent. A countervailing duty order requires a deposit equal to eight percent of entered value. Assume a 0.3464 percent ad valorem MPF within the statutory range. What total amount is owed including the deposit?

options.A: $610.06, the ordinary duty and the merchandise processing fee alone on the entry
options.B: $2,600.00, the ordinary duty and the countervailing deposit alone on this entry
options.C: $2,690.06, the ordinary duty, the countervailing deposit, and the processing fee
options.D: $4,770.06, the countervailing deposit counted twice along with the other amounts due

question: Imported maple syrup is moved into a bonded warehouse and later sold to a domestic distributor in the United States without ever being exported or destroyed. The importer asks whether a drawback claim is available for the duty paid. Which statement applies?

options.A: Drawback requires a later export or destruction, so the claim is not available.
options.B: Drawback applies because bonded warehouse storage is treated as a form of export
options.C: Drawback applies if the goods remain in the warehouse for one full calendar year
options.D: Drawback applies only if the importer later exports an equal quantity of goods

question: A broker owns a significant share of the freight forwarder handling a client's shipment, and reporting a lower entered value would reduce the client's costs and increase the forwarder's chances of keeping the account. The broker is tempted to accept the client's undervalued invoice. What duty governs this situation?

options.A: The broker's ownership share must be disclosed only if the client asks about it directly
options.B: A financial interest must not influence the accuracy of information reported to CBP
options.C: The broker may rely on the invoice because the client provided the valuation figures for it
options.D: The broker may accept the invoice if the forwarder's service fee is separately invoiced

question: A broker is completing the line-item area for a shipment of imported ceramic floor tile with a quantity of nine hundred kilograms and an entered value of forty thousand dollars. The HTSUS provision states a duty of three percent of value plus twenty cents per kilogram. What amount belongs in column 35 as the duty on this line?

options.A: $1,200.00, the three percent ad valorem portion of the compound rate by itself here
options.B: $1,380.00, the compound duty combining the percentage and per kilogram amounts
options.C: $180.00, the twenty cents per kilogram portion of the compound rate by itself
options.D: $2,580.00, a six percent rate plus the per kilogram amount shown on the line

question: An importer receives palm kernel oil that fails the contracted free fatty acid specification, uses the oil anyway in a soap production run, and then seeks rejected merchandise drawback. The oil was never returned to CBP custody. What is the likely outcome?

options.A: The claim fails because the goods were used and were not returned, exported, or destroyed.
options.B: The claim succeeds because the oil was defective when it arrived at the soap plant
options.C: The claim succeeds as substitution manufacturing drawback instead of rejected merchandise drawback
options.D: The claim fails only because a textile visa was not obtained for the shipment at the port of entry

question: An importer brings in a camping cook set packaged as one retail unit that contains a portable gas stove, two aluminum cooking pots, a folding spatula, and a carry bag. The stove is the highest value item and the article buyers identify with the product. Under the General Rules of Interpretation, how is this set classified?

options.A: Each component is classified separately under its own heading in the tariff schedule
options.B: The set is classified under the heading for the aluminum cooking pots in the set
options.C: The set is classified under the heading covering the carry bag and retail packaging
options.D: The set is classified under the heading for the portable gas stove component

question: A broker is asked to act as agent for both the importer of a shipment and the foreign seller in the same transaction, and their interests differ on the declared value. The broker considers accepting the engagement without telling either party. What does the chapter say about this kind of conflict?

options.A: The broker may act for both parties as long as the duty deposit is paid
options.B: The broker may act for both parties if the client signs a limited power of attorney
options.C: The broker may act only with full disclosure and informed consent of all parties
options.D: The broker may act for both parties because customs business is purely administrative

question: A client asks why Congress allows drawback refunds at all, given that duty was lawfully collected when imported industrial dye entered the country. The broker explains the policy behind 19 USC 1313. Which explanation matches the chapter's rationale for drawback?

options.A: The United States does not want to keep duty on goods that leave the country.
options.B: The United States refunds duty to reward importers for buying domestic raw materials.
options.C: CBP refunds duty whenever an importer files more than one entry per year.
options.D: Congress refunds duty to offset the cost of filing drawback paperwork.

question: A broker is entering a shipment of imported rubber hose that carries a specific duty of dollars per kilogram rather than a percentage rate. The broker has both the gross weight and the net weight available in the shipment documents and must choose the figure that actually drives the duty. Which column supplies that figure?

options.A: Column 30, which reports the gross weight of the merchandise entered
options.B: Column 31, which reports the manifest quantity shown for the shipment on file
options.C: Column 32, which reports net quantity in the HTSUS units used for duty
options.D: Column 33, which reports the entered value declared by the importer of record

question: A purchase order sets a single delivered price of sixty-two thousand dollars for imported industrial pumps, described on the commercial invoice as covering the goods delivered to the US port. The invoice contains no separate line for transportation or insurance. What entered value should the broker report for this shipment?

options.A: $58,000, after subtracting an estimated freight and insurance amount from the stated delivered price
options.B: $64,500, after adding an estimated freight and insurance amount to the stated price
options.C: $60,000, after deducting a standard freight allowance from the delivered price quoted
options.D: $62,000, because the transportation cost was not separately identified for deduction

question: Two clients both export imported wool carpet without using it. One client returns carpet that failed the purchase specification, and the other exports carpet that met the order because demand fell. The broker must classify each transaction. Which fact distinguishes rejected merchandise drawback from unused merchandise drawback?

options.A: Whether the export was triggered by a nonconformity or by ordinary business reasons.
options.B: Whether the carpet was stored in a bonded warehouse before the export sale
options.C: Whether the importing country and the exporting country share a free trade agreement at the border
options.D: Whether the exported carpet was entered under a specific quota category number at entry

question: A broker lets a filing deadline pass on a client's entry, and the client later asks what harm can result from the delay. According to the chapter's discussion of the duty of timeliness, what exposure does a missed deadline create for the client?

options.A: A refund of any duty already deposited with CBP on the entry in question
options.B: Liquidated damages, penalties, or loss of a preferential program
options.C: Automatic extension of the deadline by the same number of calendar days
options.D: Transfer of the broker's license to another qualified employee at the firm

question: A broker is preparing an informal entry for a low-value shipment of imported stationery and needs to calculate the merchandise processing fee before finalizing the total owed. Which statement correctly describes how the MPF works for an informal entry compared with a formal entry?

options.A: An informal entry pays the same ad valorem percentage used for formal entries
options.B: An informal entry pays the ad valorem percentage without any minimum or maximum
options.C: An informal entry pays a flat fee amount rather than a percentage of value
options.D: An informal entry pays no merchandise processing fee under any circumstances

question: A producer in Ontario claims USMCA preference for laboratory glassware assembled from United States and Mexican inputs. The applicable rule requires a regional value content calculation, and the producer asks which methods USMCA allows for that calculation. Which answer matches the chapter?

options.A: The transaction value method and the net cost method, each with its own threshold.
options.B: The first sale method and the fallback method used in customs valuation practice
options.C: The tariff shift method and the de minimis method combined into a single formula
options.D: The same kind and quality test used for the manufacturing drawback claims here at entry

question: An importer pays forty-eight thousand dollars for a shipment of decorative lamps and separately pays a selling commission of twenty-four hundred dollars to the foreign seller's agent. International freight of three thousand dollars appears as its own line on the invoice. What entered value should the broker declare?

options.A: $48,000, the invoice price without any of the additional charges included
options.B: $50,400, the invoice price plus the selling commission paid to the agent
options.C: $51,000, the invoice price with the separately identified freight amount added
options.D: $53,400, the invoice price with the commission and the freight both added

question: A broker is preparing the header of CBP Form 7501 for a routine shipment that has been released into the commerce of the United States, and the client asks which entry type code belongs in that header field. Under the entry type codes described in this chapter, which code identifies a consumption entry?

options.A: 11, the entry type code commonly used for a formal warehouse withdrawal
options.B: 01, the entry type code used for a consumption entry filed with CBP
options.C: 21, the entry type code commonly used for a temporary importation bond
options.D: 31, the entry type code commonly used for an informal mail shipment

question: A broker advises a client to pay the over-quota duty on kitchen knives that are actually subject to an absolute quota, believing a higher rate will secure release. The client follows the advice and files the entry. What is the likely consequence described in the chapter?

options.A: CBP will release the goods after collecting the higher over-quota duty rate
options.B: CBP will prorate the entry against the remaining absolute quota quantity available here at the border
options.C: CBP will treat the entry as a tariff-rate quota entry and bill the duty difference later
options.D: CBP will not release the entry, because an absolute quota has no duty-rate workaround.

question: A client wants to know whether origin analysis still matters for polyester sleeping bags now that broad textile quotas have ended. The sleeping bags are produced in a country that is not part of a free trade agreement with the United States. What does the chapter say about origin analysis?

options.A: Origin analysis is unnecessary because textile quotas were eliminated worldwide in the year 2005
options.B: Origin analysis applies only when the sleeping bags enter the country under a quota category at the port
options.C: Textile trade remains subject to detailed rules of origin even where quotas no longer apply.
options.D: Origin analysis applies only to apparel made from cotton or wool fibers alone

question: An importer receives a shipment of leather work boots that fails to meet the contracted size specification and returns the lot to the foreign supplier. The importer wants to file a rejected merchandise drawback claim. Besides proving the nonconformity and the export, which additional condition does the chapter emphasize?

options.A: Timely notice to CBP and proper handling of the merchandise under the regulatory conditions.
options.B: A binding ruling from the Office of Trade before the goods may move from the port at the port of entry
options.C: A textile visa endorsement issued by the exporting country's government abroad at entry
options.D: Payment of the full over-quota duty rate on the returned merchandise at the port at entry

question: A broker's client cannot enter a shipment of sheepskin leather gloves because the absolute quota is closed, so the client moves the goods into a foreign trade zone. The client asks whether the gloves can be sold into the United States from the zone during the same quota period. What is the correct answer?

options.A: The gloves may be sold domestically once the foreign trade zone is activated at the port of entry
options.B: The gloves may be sold domestically if the importer pays the higher over-quota rate
options.C: The gloves cannot enter United States commerce until quota room becomes available again.
options.D: The gloves may be sold domestically after CBP prorates the shipment among the importers

question: A manufacturer claims direct identification manufacturing drawback on imported lithium battery chargers built into power stations that are exported to Panama. CBP's auditor asks what documentation the chapter says typically supports this traceable link between entry and export. Which answer matches the chapter?

options.A: A textile visa endorsed by the country that originally exported the chargers
options.B: A certification of origin signed by the foreign producer of the battery chargers at the port
options.C: A quota category number assigned by CBP's Office of Trade to the entry file here
options.D: Production records, bills of materials, and inventory accounting showing the link.

question: An importer enters a lot of cheddar cheese while quota room remains under the applicable tariff-rate quota. The entry summary reports the lower in-quota rate shown in the Harmonized Tariff Schedule. A later shipment of the same cheese arrives after the quota quantity is filled. What rate applies to the later shipment?

options.A: The higher over-quota rate listed for the same tariff provision in the HTSUS.
options.B: The same in-quota rate, because both shipments share a single tariff provision
options.C: No duty, because cheese is exempt from duty once the quota period has started at the border
options.D: A penalty rate set by the port director for late quota arrivals at the port

question: Imported aircraft rivets are found defective at importation and cannot be returned to the foreign supplier because the cost of shipping exceeds their value. The importer arranges destruction under CBP supervision after proper notice. Which drawback provision can cover the destroyed rivets?

options.A: Unused merchandise drawback under section 1313(j), because the rivets were not installed in an aircraft at the port of entry here
options.B: Rejected merchandise drawback under section 1313(c), because defective goods were destroyed under supervision.
options.C: Substitution manufacturing drawback under section 1313(b), because other rivets were available in the distributor's stock
options.D: No drawback, because rejected merchandise must be exported to a foreign buyer abroad

question: An experienced client asks who decides how much of a particular dairy product may enter the United States under a quota, thinking that CBP sets the allowed amount each year. Which answer correctly describes where those quota quantities come from?

options.A: CBP's Office of Trade sets the quantity each year after consulting with the affected importers
options.B: The port director sets the quantity based on the available warehouse space at the port at the port
options.C: The exporting country's government sets the quantity through a bilateral textile visa arrangement
options.D: Congress, a presidential proclamation, or an international agreement establishes the quantity.

question: A buyer purchases imported bulk cider from the original importer and then exports that cider to a customer in Ireland. The original importer wants drawback and asks whether the documentation chain can be established. Which principle of drawback governs this claim?

options.A: Drawback is available only to the party that physically performed the export of the goods at the port of entry
options.B: The claimant must establish the chain connecting the imported merchandise to the later export.
options.C: Drawback is unavailable because a domestic sale broke the original import chain at the port
options.D: Drawback is available only if the cider was destroyed rather than exported abroad at the port

question: A manufacturer exported frozen french fries made partly from imported potatoes but discarded the production and inventory records that established the import to export link. CBP now questions the claim. Which statement reflects the chapter's view of the claimant's burden?

options.A: The claimant may rely on CBP's own entry records and need not keep production data.
options.B: The claimant may substitute an affidavit from a warehouse employee for missing records.
options.C: The claimant may refile the claim as rejected merchandise drawback instead.
options.D: The claimant must establish the necessary chain and proof with supporting records.

question: A distributor receives a container of industrial centrifugal pumps that it did not order. The foreign supplier shipped the container by mistake, and the distributor refuses the delivery and arranges the return. The pumps matched no order and duties were paid when the container entered. Which drawback basis fits this return?

options.A: Rejected merchandise drawback under section 1313(c), because the shipment was made without the consignee's consent.
options.B: Unused merchandise drawback under section 1313(j), because the pumps were not placed into service by the distributor
options.C: Manufacturing drawback under section 1313(b), because pumps are assembled articles of commerce made abroad for sale
options.D: Substitution unused merchandise drawback under section 1313(j), because similar pumps were in the distributor's own stock

question: A customs broker is training new staff on the three fact patterns that trigger rejected merchandise drawback under section 1313(c). The trainee asks which situations qualify, aside from nonconformity to specification. Which list matches the chapter's description of the three triggers?

options.A: Late arrival, short shipment, and damaged packaging discovered after the entry was filed
options.B: Shipment without the consignee's consent and merchandise found defective at importation.
options.C: Merchandise that lost value because the market price fell after arrival in the country at the border
options.D: Merchandise that was entered under a tariff-rate quota and exceeded the quota quantity

question: A broker is summarizing her drawback practice for a new client who imports cocoa butter and exports several unrelated product lines. The client asks which practical duties the broker manages for drawback clients. Which list matches the chapter's practical takeaways?

options.A: Confirm quota openings, obtain textile visas, and file the correct quota category numbers at entry
options.B: Calculate regional value content, apply tariff shifts, and certify the goods' country of origin for the goods
options.C: Identify the applicable 1313 category, apply the 8-digit standard, and track the five year window.
options.D: Set duty rates, publish quota bulletins, and approve the refund amounts for CBP at the port

question: A broker claims USMCA preferential treatment for imported goods and later receives a request from Customs for records supporting the claim. The importer asks what obligation attaches to the party claiming the preference. What does the chapter state about that obligation?

options.A: The importer claiming preference must exercise reasonable care and produce supporting records
options.B: The exporter alone must retain the supporting records and the importer has no obligation for the entry
options.C: The producer must provide records only when Customs issues a formal subpoena for them
options.D: The importer must refile the entry before any supporting records may be requested by Customs

question: A chemical trading company brings in titanium dioxide pigment and sells it domestically, then later exports an equal quantity of domestically produced pigment under the same 8-digit subheading. The company wants drawback for the exported pigment, arguing it stands in for the imports. Which drawback concept does this reflect?

options.A: Direct identification unused merchandise drawback under section 1313(j).
options.B: Substitution unused merchandise drawback under section 1313(j), using the same subheading standard.
options.C: Rejected merchandise drawback under section 1313(c), because the exports replaced imports.
options.D: Direct identification manufacturing drawback under section 1313(a), because the imports were traced.

question: A broker is about to file an entry for cotton bath towels that fall under an absolute quota. The broker wants to confirm the procedural step the chapter identifies for quota merchandise before the goods can be counted against the quota. Which step is required?

options.A: Submit a paper visa issued by the United States to the exporting country's customs office.
options.B: Obtain a binding ruling from the Office of Trade before the vessel arrives.
options.C: Post a continuous bond equal to twice the value of the quota shipment.
options.D: File the entry summary at a port of entry so quota status can be checked electronically.

question: A broker is preparing to present quota merchandise for entry and must confirm the conditions that must be satisfied. The client asks what must be true about the goods themselves before presentation can occur. What does the chapter require about the goods?

options.A: The merchandise must have arrived within the port limits before presentation
options.B: The merchandise must already be sold to a United States purchaser before entry
options.C: The merchandise must be covered by a foreign government export visa at entry
options.D: The merchandise must first be placed in a bonded warehouse or foreign trade zone

question: A broker is advising a client on the timing of a condensed milk shipment that may be subject to a quota. The broker wants to confirm the current quota status and opening dates before recommending a shipping schedule. Where does the chapter say that quota status and opening date information is published?

options.A: In the Harmonized Tariff Schedule, under the general notes for each chapter.
options.B: In the Quota Bulletin published by CBP's Office of Trade.
options.C: In the Federal Register, in a notice issued by the port director.
options.D: In the importer's continuous bond rider filed with the port.

question: A first time drawback claimant asks the broker where a refund request for exported polypropylene rope should be filed, and what the claimant must be ready to show when CBP reviews it. Which response matches the chapter's description of drawback claims?

options.A: Claims are filed with the Department of Commerce and supported by a bill of lading.
options.B: Claims are filed with the foreign buyer's government and supported by a visa.
options.C: Claims are filed with CBP and supported by a chain linking imports to the export.
options.D: Claims are filed with the port director and supported by a quota category number.

question: A broker prepares a drawback package and must decide what the claim itself has to establish. The client asks what evidence Customs expects beyond the export documentation alone when the claim is filed. What does the chapter require the claimant to establish for the package?

options.A: A traced chain from import to export along with proof duty was paid
options.B: Only that the goods left the country within the same calendar year as import
options.C: A quota category number matching the entry that was originally filed
options.D: A ruling from Customs confirming classification before the export occurs

question: An importer destroys imported empty tin cans at a scrap yard without notifying CBP or arranging supervision. The importer later files an unused merchandise drawback claim for the destroyed cans, arguing the cans were never used in the United States. What is the likely result of the claim?

options.A: The claim succeeds because destroyed goods need no supervision by CBP
options.B: The claim succeeds if the importer provides photographs of the destruction process
options.C: The claim fails because the destruction did not occur under CBP supervision.
options.D: The claim converts to rejected merchandise drawback automatically upon filing

question: A client's file references the statutory section that provides the foundation for drawback refunds, and the client asks what that citation covers. The broker must identify the provision. Which citation does the chapter give as the statutory foundation for drawback?

options.A: Section 1313 of title 19, which is the statutory foundation for drawback
options.B: The regulation that governs the presentation of quota merchandise at a port
options.C: The proclamation that fixes the quota quantity for a sensitive commodity
options.D: The agreement text that sets the rules of origin for USMCA goods

question: Imported optical lenses are installed in laboratory instruments, used for a year in the importer's testing lab, then removed and exported with the instruments. The importer files an unused merchandise drawback claim on the exported lenses. How should the claim be treated?

options.A: The claim is valid because the lenses left the country in a fully workable state
options.B: The claim is valid if the lenses were exported within five years of their importation
options.C: The claim converts to rejected merchandise drawback because the lenses were later removed at the port of entry
options.D: The claim fails because used merchandise does not qualify as unused merchandise drawback.

question: A broker discovers that a client's drawback claim on imported graphite electrodes was never filed, and the merchandise was imported six years and two months ago. The underlying export and payment records are complete. What is the outcome under the standard filing window described in the chapter?

options.A: CBP may accept the claim because the records are complete and accurate for the entry
options.B: The refund right is forfeited because the five year filing window has passed.
options.C: The claim may be filed within ten years when the exporter is also the manufacturer
options.D: The claim may proceed if the importer pays a late filing penalty to CBP

question: A company imports finished consumer goods, stores them in a warehouse without processing, and later exports some of the same unopened units because domestic demand fell short of forecast. The broker must identify the correct drawback category. Which provision applies here?

options.A: Unused merchandise drawback, which applies to goods exported in the same condition
options.B: Manufacturing drawback, because the goods were held in a warehouse before the export occurred
options.C: Rejected merchandise drawback, because the goods did not sell as the importer expected
options.D: Substitution drawback under section 1313(c) for nonconforming imported merchandise

question: CBP questions a drawback claim for imported printed circuit boards that were later exported. The broker must explain how the boards in the export shipment connect to the original import entry. Which element must the broker establish to support the refund?

options.A: The foreign buyer's end use of the circuit boards after the export sale at the port of entry
options.B: The profit margin earned by the importer on the export sale transaction at entry
options.C: The carrier's schedule for the vessel that moved the exported cargo abroad at the port
options.D: A chain connecting the imported merchandise or its substitute to the later export.

question: A client asks what a drawback refund actually includes when imported copper wire rod, or a substitute for it, is later exported or destroyed under CBP supervision. The broker should explain the scope of the refund. Which description matches the chapter's statement of what drawback refunds?

options.A: Only the ad valorem duty, with taxes and fees excluded from any refund.
options.B: The full purchase price of the merchandise plus the duty paid at entry.
options.C: Duties, taxes, and certain fees paid on the imported merchandise.
options.D: The duty plus interest from the date of entry at the market rate.

question: A broker maintains a list of countries eligible for GSP treatment and updates it only at the start of each year. A colleague warns that this practice is risky. What reason does the chapter give for treating country eligibility as changeable?

options.A: A country may be removed for graduation, competitive need limits, or policy reasons
options.B: Eligibility changes only when a country signs a new free trade agreement with the United States
options.C: Eligibility rotates among beneficiary countries on a fixed three-year cycle of review
options.D: Eligibility changes only when the quota bulletin closes for that particular country

question: A fluid power distributor claims substitution drawback on exported hydraulic valves, but the imported valves and the exported valves are classified under different 8-digit HTSUS subheadings. The distributor argues the valves are commercially similar and used for the same purpose. Under the TFTEA-based substitution standard, what is the result?

options.A: The claim succeeds because commercial similarity replaces tariff classification in the test
options.B: The claim fails because substitution requires the same 8-digit HTSUS subheading.
options.C: The claim succeeds if the importer exports twice the imported quantity of valves
options.D: The claim fails only if CBP first issues a penalty for the misclassification

question: A broker is assembling a drawback claim for imported denim trousers that were later exported. A supervisor says the Trade Facilitation and Trade Enforcement Act of 2015 affects how claims are submitted and recorded. Which change should the broker expect when filing the claim?

options.A: Paper claims must be filed at the port where the goods were originally entered
options.B: Claims must be filed within one year of export rather than within five years
options.C: Substitution is judged by the commercially interchangeable standard alone at the border
options.D: Claims must be filed electronically in CBP's Automated Commercial Environment.

question: A broker is updating training notes on the North American agreement that governs origin for goods from Mexico and Canada. The notes need the date the agreement that replaced NAFTA entered into force. Which effective date should the broker record?

options.A: July 1, 2020, when the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement entered into force
options.B: January 1, 1994, when the North American Free Trade Agreement took effect
options.C: January 1, 2005, when textile quotas were eliminated worldwide by the World Trade Organization
options.D: July 1, 2015, when the Trade Facilitation and Trade Enforcement Act passed

question: A broker is preparing to present butter subject to an absolute quota that opens at a stated hour on the first day of the quota period. The broker wants to know which filings count as simultaneously presented for proration. According to the chapter, what determines whether entries are treated as presented at the opening?

options.A: Whether the vessel arrived within the port limits before the quota opened under established CBP practice
options.B: Whether the importer paid the estimated duties before the quota opened for the entry
options.C: Whether the goods were unloaded from the vessel container before the quota opening hour at the port
options.D: Whether the entry was actually filed with CBP under the port's quota procedures at that time.

question: Three importers each present an entry for milk protein concentrate at the same opening moment for an absolute quota that has room left for only one shipment. Each entry is complete and timely. CBP applies the proration rule described in the chapter. What is the likely result?

options.A: The first entry filed receives the entire remaining quota quantity then available at that port
options.B: All three entries are rejected and the goods must be exported or destroyed at the importer's expense
options.C: The available quantity is divided proportionally among the entries presented at the same time.
options.D: CBP holds a lottery and awards the quota quantity to one of the three competing importers

question: A broker is training a new employee and explains the historical textile visa system that once governed cotton knit shirts shipped under bilateral quota agreements. The employee asks what the visa actually was. Which statement correctly describes the historical textile visa?

options.A: A travel document issued to the importing broker by the United States government at entry
options.B: An endorsement or export authorization issued by the exporting country's government.
options.C: A customs bond posted by the importer to secure payment of any quota charges
options.D: A certificate of origin issued by a domestic chamber of commerce abroad at the port of entry

question: An older drawback file from 2010 involves unused imported PVC resin pellets that were substituted with domestic resin. The broker must describe the substitution standard that applied before the Trade Facilitation and Trade Enforcement Act of 2015 changed the test. Which standard applied then?

options.A: The same 8-digit HTSUS subheading test, which the statute already required in the year 2010 under the tariff statute
options.B: The tariff shift test drawn from the USMCA rules of origin text for goods for goods
options.C: The regional value content test used for free trade agreement origin claims at entry
options.D: The commercially interchangeable standard applied to unused merchandise substitution claims.

question: An importer of finished apparel asks about an old file that references a textile visa issued by the government of the exporting country. The importer assumes it was a travel document for a company representative who visited the factory. What should the broker clarify?

options.A: It was an export authorization certifying the shipment counted against that country's quota
options.B: It was a travel document issued to the exporter's production managers for factory site visits abroad
options.C: It was a payment guarantee issued by the importing country's central bank to the seller
options.D: It was a health certificate confirming the fabric met United States safety rules at entry

question: A cosmetics maker imports fragrance compounds and also buys compounds of the same 8-digit HTSUS subheading from a New Jersey supplier. Both are blended with alcohol into cologne that is exported to South Korea, and the maker cannot trace which drums went into which bottles. Production records document the quantities. Which drawback provision applies?

options.A: Direct identification manufacturing drawback under section 1313(a), because drums can be matched to individual bottles
options.B: Unused merchandise drawback under section 1313(j), because the compounds were not sold in the domestic market
options.C: Rejected merchandise drawback under section 1313(c), because the formula was revised before the export run
options.D: Substitution manufacturing drawback under section 1313(b), because mixed inputs produced the exported article.

question: A beverage distributor imports green coffee beans and holds a large fungible inventory that mixes lots from several countries. The distributor wants to export beans regularly to foreign customers without tracking each individual lot back to a specific import entry. Which feature of unused merchandise drawback makes that practical?

options.A: Direct identification, which requires tracing each unit back to its original import entry
options.B: The five year filing window, which removes any need for detailed shipping or inventory records
options.C: Substitution, which allows interchangeable merchandise to stand in for the imported goods.
options.D: Rejected merchandise treatment, which covers goods of unacceptable quality to buyers at retail

question: Three importers present quota entries at the same opening moment, and the remaining quota room is only large enough for one of the shipments. One broker submitted a few seconds earlier than the others and expects to receive the whole remaining amount. How does Customs handle this?

options.A: Customs prorates the remaining quantity among the entries presented at the same time
options.B: Customs awards the entire remaining quantity to the entry it received first at the port
options.C: Customs rejects all three entries and requires each importer to refile in the next period
options.D: Customs holds a lottery among the three entries to decide which shipment enters

question: A metals firm imports aluminum ingots and melts them into extruded window frames that are sold to a builder in Germany. Production records tie each exported frame bundle to specific import entries of the ingots. The firm wants the most defensible classification for its refund claim. Which drawback provision applies?

options.A: Unused merchandise drawback under section 1313(j), because the metal was not consumed domestically anywhere in the United States
options.B: Rejected merchandise drawback under section 1313(c), because the frames differ from the imported ingots in form
options.C: Direct identification manufacturing drawback under section 1313(a), because traced imports became exported articles.
options.D: Substitution unused merchandise drawback under section 1313(j), because ingots and frames differ in form and tariff terms

question: A medical supply distributor imports nitrile examination gloves from Malaysia and stores the pallets in a climate controlled warehouse. A hospital chain in Brazil later buys 2,000 cases, and the distributor ships the same untampered pallets it received. Entry records match the exported cases to one import entry. Which drawback claim is correct?

options.A: Manufacturing drawback under section 1313(b), because the gloves were repacked for export to a foreign hospital buyer
options.B: Direct identification unused merchandise drawback under section 1313(j), because traced imports were re-exported unchanged.
options.C: Substitution unused merchandise drawback under section 1313(j), because any examination glove could be substituted into the claim
options.D: Rejected merchandise drawback under section 1313(c), because the Brazilian buyer paid a much lower price for the cases at the port

question: During a compliance meeting, a client asks which federal agency decides how large an annual quota will be for a sensitive agricultural commodity. The client wants to know whether the same office that processes the entries also sets the volume. What should the broker explain?

options.A: Quota volumes come from statute, proclamation, or agreement while Customs administers them
options.B: Customs and Border Protection sets each quota volume each year after reviewing prior import volumes
options.C: The Department of Commerce fixes the quota volumes each year and Customs only collects the duty
options.D: Quota volumes are negotiated each year by the importing broker community with Customs officials

question: A wholesaler imports 40,000 stainless steel ball bearings of a standard size and later exports 15,000 bearings of that same size drawn from a mixed warehouse pool that holds imported and domestic bearings. The company cannot trace individual bearings to a particular entry, but inventory records show all units share one 8-digit HTSUS subheading. Which drawback rule applies?

options.A: Direct identification unused merchandise drawback under section 1313(j), because the bearings stayed unused in the warehouse pool
options.B: Manufacturing drawback under section 1313(a), because bearings are components of assembled machinery in the plant
options.C: Substitution unused merchandise drawback under section 1313(j), because same subheading merchandise was exported.
options.D: Rejected merchandise drawback under section 1313(c), because the order quantity was reduced by the foreign buyer

question: A broker's client imports 12,000 square meters of glazed ceramic floor tiles from Spain and stores them untouched in a Memphis warehouse. Eight months later the client sells 5,000 square meters to a buyer in Jamaica and ships them out. The client can trace the exported tiles to the specific import entry. Which drawback provision applies?

options.A: Rejected merchandise drawback under section 1313(c), because the buyer changed the order.
options.B: Manufacturing drawback under section 1313(a), because the tiles were stored for months.
options.C: Unused merchandise drawback under section 1313(j), because the tiles left in the same condition.
options.D: Substitution manufacturing drawback under section 1313(b), because another tile lot was available.

question: An importer's shipment of imported guitar strings is excepted from individual article marking under 19 CFR 134.32 due to impracticality, and the outer retail package is properly marked instead. The importer later repacks the strings into unmarked bulk bins for wholesale distribution without notifying CBP. What compliance failure does this create?

options.A: A violation of the repacking certification and marking obligation under 19 CFR 134.26, since the new bulk containers were not marked and no certification was filed
options.B: No violation exists because the original exception under 134.32 covers any future repackaging of the strings at the facility
options.C: The importer satisfies the marking law simply because the individual guitar strings were excepted from marking requirements
options.D: Repacking the strings into wholesale bulk bins for wholesale distribution is outside of CBP regulatory jurisdiction at any port of entry

question: A broker is preparing for a quota opening scheduled at a stated hour, when many importers will try to enter against a limited quantity. The broker needs to understand how Customs treats entries presented around that moment. What does the chapter explain?

options.A: Entries are ranked by the exact second the broker transmits the entry data to Customs
options.B: Entries are accepted only from brokers registered at that specific port of entry
options.C: Entries are held until Customs auctions the remaining quota quantity to importers at the port
options.D: Entries treated as simultaneously presented are prorated against available quantity

question: A broker is preparing a study plan for the licensing exam and wants to organize the chapter's closing message about subjects that must be understood together. Which three subjects does the chapter identify as interlocking because they affect duty and entry outcomes?

options.A: Entry filing, classification, and liquidation of the entry summary
options.B: Quota limits, preferential trade programs, and drawback refunds
options.C: Valuation, country of origin marking, and importer recordkeeping requirements
options.D: Administrative penalties, protests, and judicial review of Customs decisions

question: A shipment of imported cast metal figurines arrives with the country of origin embossed directly into the metal base of each figurine in a location that is visible but requires the purchaser to turn the figurine upside down to read it clearly. Is this placement likely acceptable under CBP marking standards?

options.A: It can be acceptable if an ordinary purchaser examining the figurine under normal conditions would reasonably find and read the marking, even if turning the item is required
options.B: It is automatically unacceptable any time the marking requires any physical manipulation of the article in order for an ordinary buyer to read the marking clearly on the packaging
options.C: Placement is irrelevant because an embossed metal marking is considered inherently conspicuous under the applicable federal marking rules and CBP guidance at the port of entry
options.D: Base marking is not permitted for decorative articles, no matter how accessible it is to the ordinary purchaser examining the goods on a retail display shelf

question: A different broker makes the opposite mistake and advises a client that an absolute quota can be entered over the limit by paying the higher second-tier duty rate. What does the chapter say can result from that mistaken advice when the entry is filed?

options.A: The merchandise will be entered at the second tier rate after a ruling is issued
options.B: An entry that Customs will not release, because no duty rate opens the ceiling
options.C: The merchandise will be admitted once the importer posts a double duty bond
options.D: The merchandise will be entered at the in-quota rate until the quota reopens

question: A broker is timing an import of a commodity covered by a tariff rate quota with a substantially higher over-quota rate. The client asks when the lower in-quota rate will apply to the shipment. Which answer is correct under the chapter?

options.A: The in-quota rate applies to every entry once a preference claim is filed
options.B: The in-quota rate applies to merchandise entered while quota room remains
options.C: The in-quota rate applies only to merchandise entered after the quota fills
options.D: The in-quota rate applies only to merchandise from free trade agreement partners

question: A trademark holder discovers that CBP seized a shipment of counterfeit goods and wants to know whether it may be entitled to receive samples or information about the seized goods to support a related civil trademark infringement lawsuit against the importer. What is generally true about this type of disclosure under CBP procedures?

options.A: CBP procedures allow limited disclosure of certain information and samples to trademark owners to assist in pursuing civil remedies against infringers
options.B: Civil lawsuits against importers of counterfeit goods are legally impossible once CBP has already seized the counterfeit merchandise at the port
options.C: Trademark owners automatically receive a full ownership transfer of all of the seized counterfeit merchandise for any purpose or use that they choose
options.D: CBP is prohibited from sharing information about a seizure with the affected trademark owner during its enforcement process

question: A broker is preparing documentation for merchandise subject to an absolute quota that will be entered at a seaport. The client asks where the entry summary paperwork must be filed and how quota status is verified. What does the chapter describe?

options.A: The entry summary is filed with the carrier, which reports the quota status to Customs
options.B: The entry summary is filed at the foreign port before the vessel departs the foreign port
options.C: The entry summary is filed with the quota holder named in the applicable presidential proclamation
options.D: The entry summary is filed at a port of entry, and quota status is checked electronically

question: A broker is studying historical quota practice to prepare for questions about how programs have changed over time. The chapter notes that some product groups once operated under absolute quota limits. Which groups are named for that history in the chapter?
