options.A: Certain fresh vegetables, cut flowers, and unroasted coffee arriving by air
options.B: Certain dairy products and a number of textile categories
options.C: Passenger automobiles, light trucks, and most imported automotive components
options.D: Refined petroleum products, natural gas, and coal delivered by pipeline

question: An importer of imported eyeglass frames wants to place the country of origin marking on the inside of the temple arm, a location not immediately visible unless the frame is opened and examined closely. Is this placement likely to satisfy the conspicuousness standard for an ultimate purchaser browsing a retail display?

options.A: It may fail conspicuousness if an ordinary purchaser examining the frame under normal retail conditions would not readily notice the marking in that location
options.B: Any location on the article automatically satisfies the conspicuousness standard as long as the origin marking exists somewhere on the article or its packaging
options.C: The conspicuousness standard applies only to bulk shipping containers and not to the marking on the retail article or its packaging
options.D: Placement is irrelevant to conspicuousness as long as the marking text itself is grammatically correct and clearly legible to ordinary buyers

question: A broker is about to advise a client to claim GSP treatment on an entry and wants to confirm the program's current legal status. A colleague reminds the broker that this check is necessary. Why is this confirmation required for the entry?

options.A: GSP eligibility is decided by each port director at the time of each entry
options.B: GSP applies only when the merchandise also qualifies under the USMCA rules
options.C: GSP authorization is not permanent and the program has periodically lapsed
options.D: GSP requires a presidential proclamation before every individual entry at entry

question: An importer asks whether GSP will lower the duty rate on eligible merchandise or remove it entirely, and wants to know how to describe the benefit to management. How does the chapter characterize the benefit that GSP provides for eligible goods?

options.A: GSP provides a reduced rate that varies with the beneficiary country's income level
options.B: GSP grants duty free treatment to eligible merchandise from designated countries
options.C: GSP defers duty until the merchandise is sold in the domestic market at retail
options.D: GSP refunds duty after export in the same way that drawback operates for exporters

question: A recordholder notifies CBP that an imported shipment infringes its patent rights rather than its trademark or copyright, and asks how the agency would handle each situation. How does CBP's border enforcement authority for patent-based exclusion generally differ from its trademark and copyright recordation authority under Part 133?

options.A: Patent-based exclusion typically arises through International Trade Commission exclusion orders rather than the trademark and copyright e-Recordation system
options.B: Patents are recorded through the identical e-Recordation system and are enforced in exactly the same manner as trademark and copyright recordations at the border of entry
options.C: CBP has no involvement in enforcing patent-related import restrictions at the border or at any port of entry in the country
options.D: Patent enforcement at the border relies solely on state court injunctions rather than on any action or order of a federal agency or a federal court

question: During an exam style review, a broker is asked to summarize the broker's core responsibility when handling any drawback transaction for a client. Which task does the chapter identify as central to a broker's job with respect to drawback claims?

options.A: Set the duty rate that will apply to the refunded merchandise after export
options.B: Certify the origin of the imported goods under the applicable trade agreement
options.C: Identify which section 1313 category applies and track the filing deadline
options.D: Negotiate the quota quantity with the foreign government before importation

question: A drawback claimant completed a well documented export of merchandise that had been imported almost five years earlier. The claimant asks whether the claim can still be filed. What does the chapter say about the filing deadline for drawback claims?

options.A: A claim may be filed at any time while the underlying records are retained
options.B: A claim must be filed within one year from the date the goods were exported
options.C: A claim must be filed before the related entry is liquidated by Customs at the port of entry
options.D: A claim generally must be filed within five years from the date of importation

question: After reading about TFTEA, a client asks whether the modernization abolished the traditional drawback categories and replaced them with a single new claim type. The broker must correct that impression. What does the chapter say TFTEA did with those categories?

options.A: It replaced unused, manufacturing, and rejected categories with one consolidated claim
options.B: It repealed section 1313 and moved drawback authority to the trade agreements
options.C: It kept the categories intact while modernizing substitution and claim processing
options.D: It limited drawback to manufacturing claims and ended unused merchandise refunds

question: An importer's product line includes decorative key chains that are individually so small that stamping the country of origin directly onto each piece would be technically difficult and would significantly increase manufacturing cost relative to the item's value. What CBP exception might support marking only the retail packaging instead?

options.A: The exception under 19 CFR 134.32 for articles that cannot be marked except at an unreasonable expense given their nature
options.B: The exception applies only if the key chains are manufactured mainly from recycled or reclaimed materials abroad
options.C: A blanket exemption applying to all items valued under five dollars without regard to the marking feasibility for the item
options.D: There is no such exception and every article must be marked individually no matter how small it is

question: A factory draws raw material from one combined production pool holding both imported and domestically sourced goods classifiable under the same 8-digit HTSUS subheading. Finished articles are exported, but individual units cannot be traced. Which drawback provision fits these facts?

options.A: Direct identification manufacturing drawback, which requires tracing specific units to import entries
options.B: Unused merchandise drawback under section 1313(j) for goods kept in the same condition
options.C: Substitution manufacturing drawback, which relies on the substitution relationship in records
options.D: Rejected merchandise drawback under section 1313(c) for nonconforming goods imported from abroad

question: A broker is drafting a checklist for entries that may qualify for GSP treatment. The checklist must capture the three confirmations the chapter says a broker should make before advising a client on a GSP claim. Which set of checks is correct?

options.A: Confirm the visa was issued, the quota category, and the port where the goods were presented
options.B: Confirm the entry summary was filed, the duty was paid, and the goods arrived at the port of entry
options.C: Confirm the good meets a tariff shift, an RVC threshold, and the automotive content rules for vehicles
options.D: Confirm authorization is current, the country and provision are eligible, and value added is met

question: A licensed customs broker prepares an entry for imported auto parts and notices the invoice describes goods marked Assembled in USA even though all major components are foreign-made and only final bolting occurs domestically before export back to the United States after minor processing abroad. What compliance concern should the broker flag?

options.A: The marking phrase may misrepresent the true country of substantial transformation and mislead the ultimate purchaser
options.B: There is no concern because any assembly claim automatically satisfies the federal marking law
options.C: The broker has no duty to review the marking language since it falls outside the broker's usual responsibilities at entry
options.D: The phrase is acceptable as long as the invoice value stays under the informal entry value threshold for the entire shipment for the shipment

question: A manufacturer imports raw material, combines it with domestic components into a finished appliance, and ships the finished appliance to a customer abroad. The broker needs to identify the correct drawback category before filing. Which provision covers this fact pattern?

options.A: Unused merchandise drawback, because the raw material entered without any processing
options.B: Rejected merchandise drawback, because the raw material did not conform to sample
options.C: Manufacturing drawback, because imported goods were used to make an exported article
options.D: Quota drawback, because the finished appliance was entered under a tariff quota category

question: A GSP beneficiary country produces a good using materials from a neighboring country that is also a GSP beneficiary within the same regional grouping. The importer wants those materials counted toward the value added threshold. Which provision does the chapter mention?

options.A: The de minimis provision that disregards a small share of foreign content in the good
options.B: The tariff shift rule stated at the heading level of the tariff schedule at entry
options.C: Accumulation provisions specific to the regional grouping named in the program
options.D: The certification of origin data elements required for preferential duty claims at entry

question: A shipment of imported pocket knives arrives properly marked with the country of origin stamped directly into the blade in a clearly legible location. A CBP officer nonetheless questions the size of the lettering. Under 19 CFR 134.41, what standard governs the legibility of country of origin marking?

options.A: The marking must be legible and of a size reasonably found by the ordinary purchaser examining the article under normal conditions
options.B: The lettering must be at least one full inch in height no matter the overall size of the individual imported article
options.C: Legibility requirements apply only to marking placed on the outer shipping carton, not to the article or its immediate retail container
options.D: Any marking visible only under a magnifying glass satisfies the legibility standard as a matter of federal law at the time of entry

question: A client asks whether the Generalized System of Preferences is a negotiated trade agreement between the United States and beneficiary countries, similar to a free trade agreement. The broker must describe the program accurately. Which statement correctly characterizes GSP under the chapter?

options.A: GSP is a negotiated free trade agreement between the United States and each beneficiary
options.B: GSP is a unilateral program Congress authorizes by statute for designated countries
options.C: GSP is a quota program that limits how much may enter from each beneficiary
options.D: GSP is a drawback category that refunds duties on merchandise later exported

question: A broker handling automotive parts under USMCA notes that the origin analysis for these goods involves more than the usual tariff shift and regional value content review. The broker asks what additional requirements apply to automotive goods. Which answer matches the chapter?

options.A: A separate textile visa issued by the exporting country's government
options.B: A quota category number assigned by the Office of Trade
options.C: A foreign trade zone admission followed by privileged foreign status
options.D: Labor value content and steel and aluminum purchasing requirements

question: A container of imported tools includes many small items marked individually but shipped inside a corrugated carton that is not itself marked. A CBP officer questions whether the carton needs separate marking under 19 CFR 134.22. What is the correct principle governing this situation?

options.A: When each article inside is legibly and conspicuously marked, the outer container generally need not repeat the marking
options.B: Every shipping container must be marked even when the individual articles inside it are properly marked with origin
options.C: Only the innermost retail package requires marking, rather than the individual articles themselves packed inside the shipping carton
options.D: Container marking is required solely for merchandise that enters under a temporary importation bond

question: A producer asks the broker whether the regional value content threshold is the same for every product that uses an RVC rule under USMCA. The producer wants to know before structuring the bill of materials. What should the broker say about the threshold?

options.A: The threshold is identical for every product and set at fifty percent
options.B: The threshold percentage varies by product category within the agreement
options.C: The threshold applies only to agricultural goods and not to manufactured articles
options.D: The threshold is negotiated separately for each shipment by the importer

question: A manufacturer performs part of its production in Mexico and part in the United States, and wants both stages counted when measuring whether the regional value content threshold is met. Which USMCA concept allows the production from both countries to be combined?

options.A: The de minimis provision that disregards small foreign content by value
options.B: The accumulation concept that combines production from more than one party
options.C: The tariff shift rule that looks only at the finished good's classification
options.D: The certification of origin that lists the producer and exporter data

question: A shipment contains steel screws that are individually too small to be marked without impairing their function. The importer instead marks the wooden box containing the screws with the country of origin. Under what provision might this practice be permissible?

options.A: 19 CFR 134.32, the exception for articles incapable of being marked
options.B: 19 CFR 134.11, the general requirement that every article be individually marked
options.C: 19 CFR 133.21, the recordation of trademarks with Customs and Border Protection
options.D: 19 USC 1304(f), the ten percent ad valorem marking duty provision

question: An importer argues that merchandise qualifies for preferential treatment because it was shipped from a partner country and purchased from a vendor located there. The broker must explain what origin actually depends on. Which statement gives the correct legal basis for an origin determination?

options.A: The country whose flag the vessel was flying when the goods were loaded aboard the vessel at the foreign dock
options.B: The country where the vendor that sold the goods maintains its principal business office
options.C: The country where the merchandise was first offered for sale to the public at retail
options.D: Where goods were produced, grown, or manufactured and how much transformation occurred

question: A broker is explaining the general structure of origin rules that recur across United States free trade agreements. The client wants to know what the two common rule families are before looking at a specific product. Which pair does the chapter identify?

options.A: A quota category test and a visa endorsement test applied at the port
options.B: A tariff shift requirement and a regional value content requirement
options.C: A most favored nation test and a column two rate comparison
options.D: A foreign trade zone test and a bonded warehouse accounting test

question: A broker advises a client that broad textile quotas ended in 2005 and tells the client no textile rules will ever apply again. A senior broker corrects that advice. Which statement best describes what can still apply to textile and apparel trade?

options.A: Nothing may still apply, because textile restrictions ended permanently in 2005
options.B: Only the original bilateral visa program remains available for all textile shipments today
options.C: Special safeguards, country restrictions, and visa or certification rules may still appear
options.D: Textile merchandise now requires no origin analysis of any kind at the time of entry to the country

question: A broker reviewing quota status for an importer discovers that a specific tariff-rate quota is administered under a licensing arrangement with the foreign government, which changes how the first-tier quantity is allocated. Why does this detail matter to the broker's advice?

options.A: Licensing arrangements apply only to absolute quotas and not to tariff-rate quota programs
options.B: A licensing arrangement removes the over-quota rate and makes the entry duty free
options.C: Licensing arrangements are announced only in the Federal Register each January for the year
options.D: The arrangement can change the economics of a shipment significantly for the importer

question: An importer brings in unglazed clay pots that would crack if a label were pressed onto their surfaces, and marking would also destroy the delicate decorative finish. The importer asks whether the pots must be individually marked at importation. Which exception applies?

options.A: The exception for articles that would be economically or physically damaged by marking
options.B: The exception for articles imported for the personal use of the importer or the importer's household
options.C: The crude substances exception for unprocessed materials imported in bulk quantities
options.D: The exception for articles the importer will substantially transform before retail sale

question: A freight forwarder tells an importer that the consignment cannot be shipped because the tariff-rate quota for that commodity is already filled for the current year. The broker believes the forwarder has confused the quota types. What is the basis for the broker's position?

options.A: Once a tariff-rate quota fills, only merchandise from treaty partners may enter
options.B: A filled tariff-rate quota suspends entry until the next quota period opens
options.C: A filled tariff-rate quota permits entry only after a ruling is requested
options.D: Merchandise may still enter, but at the higher over-quota duty rate

question: An importer whose goods are subject to an absolute quota offers to pay any duty rate Customs wants in order to release the shipment during a closed period. The broker must explain why that offer cannot work. Which statement gives the correct reason?

options.A: Absolute quotas are closed only until the next entry summary cycle begins
options.B: A higher duty rate is available only if the importer files under another subheading
options.C: An absolute quota is controlled by quantity, so no duty rate opens the ceiling
options.D: Only the foreign exporter may request an exception from the quota ceiling

question: A domestic appliance maker imports finished heating elements from Italy and installs them into ovens it assembles in the United States. The elements are not substantially transformed before installation. The maker asks what country of origin marking the imported heating elements themselves must carry. What is the correct advice?

options.A: The elements must be marked with the foreign country of origin
options.B: The elements need no marking because the ovens are assembled in the United States
options.C: The elements must be marked as products of the United States
options.D: The elements must be marked with the country where the ovens are sold

question: A client imports a commodity listed in the tariff schedule with two different rates shown for the same provision, one lower and one higher. The broker recognizes this as a tariff-rate quota. Which statement correctly describes how the two rates apply?

options.A: The lower rate applies to all entries and the higher rate applies only to reimported goods
options.B: The lower rate applies within the quota quantity and the higher rate applies after it fills
options.C: The lower rate applies after the quota fills and the higher rate applies within the quantity
options.D: Both rates apply at the same time and the importer picks whichever is more favorable

question: A broker is refreshing knowledge of which imported products still face strict quantity ceilings rather than a two-tier duty structure. The broker recalls a canned fish product named in the chapter as a classic absolute quota example. Which commodity is that?

options.A: Certain frozen beef cuts from designated supplying countries
options.B: Certain tuna packed in airtight containers for retail sale
options.C: Raw cane sugar imported from certain designated supplying countries
options.D: Certain cheddar and other cheeses imported from Europe

question: A shipment of kitchen sponges from Vietnam arrives with no country of origin marking because the foreign supplier did not apply one. The importer tells the broker that the supplier's failure is not the importer's problem. How should the broker respond about the marking obligation?

options.A: The importer remains responsible for marking the goods before liquidation
options.B: The foreign supplier alone bears the marking duty under the statute
options.C: The importer may sell the goods unmarked if the supplier agrees in writing
options.D: The importer may defer marking until the goods reach retail shelves

question: An importer learns that a shipment subject to an absolute quota arrived after the quota closed. The importer asks the broker to list the lawful ways to handle the excess merchandise now sitting at the port under Customs custody. Which set of options is complete?

options.A: Pay the higher second-tier rate, hold the goods in a bonded warehouse, or return them
options.B: Export the goods, warehouse or zone them, or destroy them under supervision
options.C: Warehouse the goods, transship them to a third country, or reclassify them
options.D: Export the goods, sell them duty free at the port, or abandon them to Customs

question: A broker is explaining quota periods to a client who ships perishable commodities. The client asks how long a quota period typically lasts and when the quota room becomes available again after it is used up. Which answer reflects the chapter?

options.A: A quota period runs four consecutive calendar quarters in every program
options.B: A quota period runs from the date of entry until the goods are liquidated
options.C: A quota period usually runs one calendar year or a stated portion of it
options.D: A quota period runs for three years and is renewed by presidential proclamation

question: A broker is preparing a client presentation summarizing the difference between the marking duty under 19 USC 1304(f) and the trademark and copyright recordation and enforcement scheme under 19 CFR Part 133. What is the clearest way to frame this distinction for the client?

options.A: The marking duty applies only to counterfeit goods and to imported merchandise that violates the trademark rights of the owner, while Part 133 applies only to the accurately marked legitimate goods at the time of their entry into the United States at any port
options.B: Both provisions govern exactly the same subject matter and were designed to be applied interchangeably by the CBP officers at the various ports of entry during the entry, summary, and liquidation processes at the port of entry here
options.C: There is no meaningful distinction to present to the client since both frameworks produce identical remedies, penalties, and enforcement outcomes in every case presented for review under the rules for this shipment for the entry
options.D: The marking duty addresses noncompliant country of origin marking on legitimately imported goods, while Part 133 addresses detention and seizure of goods infringing recorded intellectual property rights, an entirely separate legal concern

question: A broker is preparing to advise a client on timing for a shipment covered by a quota. Before recommending a shipping date, the broker needs the current opening dates and the present status of that specific quota. Where does the broker find this official information?

options.A: In the Federal Register notices that Customs publishes after each entry is liquidated
options.B: In the entry summary instructions printed by the importing carrier for each voyage
options.C: In the Quota Bulletin published by the Office of Trade at Customs
options.D: In the Harmonized Tariff Schedule footnotes listing the in-quota duty rate only

question: A licensed customs broker learns that CBP intends to publish updated guidance clarifying acceptable abbreviations and phrases for country of origin marking. Why is it important for the broker to stay current with this type of CBP guidance for client compliance purposes?

options.A: Because marking guidance is stable over time and brokers need only learn the marking rules once at the start of their careers as customs brokers
options.B: Because marking phrase and abbreviation acceptability can evolve through CBP guidance, and outdated practices may create compliance risk for clients even if previously accepted
options.C: Because such guidance applies exclusively to foreign customs authorities and has no bearing whatsoever on the individual customs brokers licensed in the United States
options.D: Because staying current with the marking guidance is optional and has no connection to the professional responsibilities of a licensed customs broker in practice

question: A broker reviewing an importer's shipment of imported ceramic dishware sets finds that each plate, bowl, and cup is individually marked correctly, and the outer shipping carton is also marked, but the retail gift box holding a matched four-piece set together is entirely unmarked. Is the gift box itself required to bear separate marking under general principles?

options.A: No marking is required anywhere in this scenario because ceramic dishware sets are categorically exempt from the country of origin marking rules at the border for these imported ceramic goods here here today
options.B: Yes, every single layer of packaging at every level must independently repeat the full country of origin marking on every single layer without any exception whatsoever on the package in the country
options.C: Only the outer shipping carton requires marking, and individual article marking is unnecessary for imported products under the applicable federal marking rules at the border
options.D: Generally no additional marking is required on the immediate retail container when every individual article inside is already properly marked, since the purchaser will see the origin on each piece

question: An importer's imported wooden furniture arrives marked with the country of origin printed on a paper label affixed with a strong permanent adhesive that will not come off without damaging the finish, but the label is placed on the underside of the piece in a location a purchaser could examine if they looked. Is this likely compliant?

options.A: Permanent adhesive alone satisfies full compliance no matter where the label is placed on the item or how it is attached to the surface
options.B: It fails because underside placement is not permitted for furniture items under the federal marking rules at the border of entry
options.C: It is likely compliant on permanence grounds, and placement on the underside can still satisfy conspicuousness if consistent with how such furniture is normally examined by purchasers
options.D: Furniture is exempt from country of origin marking requirements, so the placement question is irrelevant to the importer of record and to the entry

question: A broker is asked to distinguish, for a new associate, the general purpose of country of origin marking law from the general purpose of intellectual property rights enforcement at the border. What is the most accurate distinction between these two bodies of law?

options.A: There is no meaningful distinction between the two and the two legal frameworks are functionally interchangeable in their application and purpose for importers and customs brokers at the border of entry into the country
options.B: Both bodies of law exist for the identical purpose of collecting revenue through duties and penalties with no other distinguishing objective whatsoever for CBP at the border of entry into the country
options.C: Marking law exists solely to benefit foreign governments and producers, while IPR enforcement exists solely to benefit domestic retailers and manufacturers in the market at the border of entry in the case today
options.D: Marking law primarily informs consumers of the true geographic origin of goods, while IPR enforcement primarily protects trademark, copyright, and patent holders from unauthorized use of their protected rights

question: A broker reviewing an importer's compliance program notes the company relies entirely on the foreign supplier's self-certification of country of origin without any independent verification, documentation review, or periodic audit. What risk does this practice create for the importer under CBP marking and origin enforcement?

options.A: Reasonable care obligations apply only to tariff classification and valuation, not to country of origin determinations made at the time of entry
options.B: The importer risks marking violations and potential penalties if the self-certified origin proves inaccurate, since reasonable care obligations extend to verifying supplier representations
options.C: CBP is legally barred from questioning the origin information once a foreign supplier has self-certified it on the entry documents for the goods
options.D: There is no risk because supplier self-certification is binding and conclusive on CBP no matter the accuracy of the certified origin information

question: A broker reviewing marking compliance for an importer's canned tuna notices the label states Wild Caught and Sustainably Sourced prominently but the required country of origin statement is printed in significantly smaller text tucked into a corner of the label. What is the appropriate compliance observation?

options.A: Marketing claims like Wild Caught take legal priority over any country of origin marking requirements under the federal marking statute
options.B: There is no compliance concern because country of origin marking is optional whenever other marketing label claims appear at the point of sale
options.C: This situation relates exclusively to food safety and nutrition labeling and has no connection whatsoever to the customs marking law or regulations at the border
options.D: The relative prominence given to the country of origin statement compared to other label claims may raise a conspicuousness concern under marking law

question: An importer's broker is asked whether goods entering a bonded warehouse for storage, without any withdrawal for domestic consumption, must be marked with the country of origin at the time they enter the warehouse. What is the correct general principle regarding marking timing relative to entry for consumption?

options.A: Marking requirements apply only to goods traveling by ocean vessel and not to goods entering a bonded warehouse for storage before later withdrawal for consumption
options.B: Marking compliance is generally assessed in connection with entry for consumption, so goods held in bond may not need to satisfy the same marking timing as goods entering domestic commerce immediately
options.C: Bonded warehouse goods are permanently exempt from needing country of origin marking under any future disposition of the goods in the United States market today
options.D: Marking is required the instant the goods physically arrive at a United States port, whatever the entry type or the ultimate disposition of the merchandise

question: A trademark owner learns that CBP seized a shipment of counterfeit goods and destroyed them after forfeiture rather than donating them to a charitable organization. Under what circumstances would CBP typically avoid donating seized counterfeit merchandise like this to a charity?

options.A: CBP is legally required to donate seized counterfeit merchandise to a charitable organization in nearly every case under the statute
options.B: Destruction of seized counterfeit goods is generally prohibited under federal law no matter the circumstances surrounding the seizure
options.C: The disposition method depends on the country of manufacture of the seized merchandise rather than on any other factor in the case
options.D: When donation would still allow the counterfeit mark to reach consumers or the trademark owner objects, destruction is generally the appropriate disposition instead

question: Cashmere scarves woven in Scotland arrive under an entry the broker is reviewing, and the broker wonders whether the general Part 134 rules are the only marking requirement for these goods. The chapter mentions additional statutes for certain goods. Which statement correctly describes how those rules apply to these scarves?

options.A: Certain textile and wool products carry additional statutory marking requirements
options.B: Textile and wool products are exempt from all country of origin marking
options.C: Textile and wool products must be marked with a paper tag on each item
options.D: Textile and wool products follow the crude substances exception

question: An importer is unsure whether raw agricultural commodities such as unprocessed coffee beans require country of origin marking under the same general framework that applies to manufactured goods brought into the country. What is the correct general principle on this point?

options.A: Agricultural commodities are categorically exempt from country of origin marking requirements under the federal customs law at the time of their entry into the country
options.B: Agricultural commodities are generally subject to the same country of origin marking framework under 19 CFR Part 134 as other imported articles, absent a specific applicable exception
options.C: Only processed or roasted coffee is subject to marking, while raw green coffee beans are excepted from the marking requirements of the statute at the border
options.D: Marking of agricultural commodities is governed by state agriculture departments rather than by the federal customs law for these goods

question: An importer brings in stainless steel flatware from South Korea and wants to know whether engraving the country of origin into the metal handle is an acceptable marking method. The engraving is legible, conspicuous, and permanent. What should the broker advise?

options.A: Engraving is acceptable because it produces a legible and permanent marking
options.B: Engraving is unacceptable because only printed labels satisfy the statute
options.C: Engraving is acceptable only after CBP approves the method in writing
options.D: Engraving is unacceptable because it damages the surface of the article

question: An importer's shipment of imported picture frames from Country A arrives with glass panes manufactured in Country B inserted into the frames before export. The frame itself, not the glass, gives the finished product its essential character and functional identity. What origin conclusion best follows from this fact pattern?

options.A: Country B, because the glass component present controls the finished article's origin despite its minor supporting role
options.B: Origin is undeterminable whenever more than one country contributes any component to a finished article
options.C: Origin must be split proportionally between both countries based on the relative material cost of each component
options.D: Country A, since the frame supplying the essential character of the finished product was manufactured and finally assembled there

question: A licensed broker is preparing entry documentation and must determine whether a component sourced from multiple countries and assembled into a finished electronic device in a single country qualifies that assembling country as the origin. What analytical approach should the broker apply?

options.A: Simply default to the country contributing the highest dollar value of components without examining where final assembly of the device occurred
options.B: Assign origin to whichever country shipped the largest single component by total weight among all the individual parts used in the assembled electronic device
options.C: Apply the substantial transformation test by evaluating whether the assembly process creates a distinct new article with a different name, character, or use
options.D: Origin is determined solely by the country listed at the very top of the commercial invoice's letterhead or header of the shipping documentation

question: A brand owner recorded its trademark with CBP years ago but the company has since changed its legal name through a corporate restructuring, though the trademark registration itself remains valid and unchanged. What should the company do to keep its CBP recordation accurate and effective?

options.A: CBP automatically updates recordation records whenever any company changes its legal name anywhere in the world
options.B: Update the CBP recordation to reflect the current legal name and ownership information associated with the mark
options.C: The company must file a new trademark application with a different mark before updating anything at CBP
options.D: Nothing is required because the CBP recordation is independent of any corporate name change made by the firm

question: A CBP officer examining an entry of imported carpets notes that the marking uses the historical name of a country that no longer exists under its current political boundaries and name, even though the correct modern country name is well established. What marking concern does this raise?

options.A: Only geography textbooks are affected by these naming conventions, not customs marking compliance or enforcement at the United States border
options.B: The marking automatically becomes correct as long as the carpet was manufactured before the political boundary change occurred in that particular region of the world
options.C: There is no concern because any historical country name is acceptable even where the modern country name is well established
options.D: The marking may be inaccurate or misleading since it should reflect the presently recognized name of the country where the goods actually originated

question: An importer's entry for imported bicycles is flagged because the frame was manufactured in one country while the wheels, gears, and brakes were manufactured elsewhere and everything was assembled into a complete, functioning bicycle in a third country. What analytical question is most central to determining origin here?

options.A: Whether the frame manufacturer's country controls the origin determination even though final assembly occurs in another country
options.B: Whether the assembly operations performed in the third country are complex enough to constitute substantial transformation of the imported components
options.C: Whether the bicycle's retail price exceeds a specific dollar threshold that triggers a different set of origin rules at entry
options.D: Whether the importer prefers one country's origin designation over another for its own promotional marketing purposes in the United States market

question: A domestic trademark owner discovers imported goods bearing an unauthorized reproduction of its mark are being sold online by a third party but never physically pass through a U.S. port of entry because they ship directly from a foreign warehouse via international mail to individual consumers. What limitation does this present for CBP-based enforcement?

options.A: International mail shipments are outside CBP jurisdiction, so the agency has no authority over those shipments at the border or at any port of entry
options.B: Online sales automatically eliminate any possibility of trademark enforcement through any government channel or agency, including CBP, at the border or in international mail shipments whatsoever
options.C: CBP has full enforcement authority over any online sale whether or not the goods ever physically enter CBP jurisdiction or reach a port of entry
options.D: CBP border enforcement generally depends on physical entry through a port or mail facility subject to CBP jurisdiction, so goods must still pass through CBP processing to be intercepted

question: A broker is asked whether an importer can satisfy the country of origin marking requirement for canned soup simply by listing the country of origin of each individual ingredient inside the can on the label, without stating a single overall country of origin for the finished product. What is the correct guidance?

options.A: Ingredient-level origin listing is required in addition to, and effectively replaces, any required finished product origin marking
options.B: No, marking law requires a single country of origin determination for the finished article as imported, not a list of individual ingredient origins
options.C: Yes, listing every ingredient's individual origin satisfies the country of origin marking requirement for processed or canned food products sold at retail
options.D: Country of origin marking does not apply to canned or processed food products at any port of entry in the country

question: A broker reviews a client's imported toy shipment and notices the marking states the country of origin correctly but is placed on the bottom of the box in extremely small font compared to the rest of the packaging graphics. What combined marking principles are potentially implicated?

options.A: No marking principle is implicated as long as the correct country name technically appears somewhere on the box
options.B: Only the permanence requirement is implicated because font size has nothing whatsoever to do with the permanence requirement
options.C: Both the legibility and conspicuousness requirements of 19 CFR 134.41 may be implicated by the placement and font size
options.D: Only the ten percent marking duty provision is implicated, with no separate legibility or conspicuousness concern

question: An importer's shipment of imported paper napkins is packaged in bulk cases intended for direct sale to restaurants, which will use the napkins without any further repackaging before customer use. Who is the ultimate purchaser for marking purposes in this business-to-business supply scenario?

options.A: The customs broker who processes the entry paperwork on behalf of the importer at the port where the entry summary is filed
options.B: The restaurant, because it is the last domestic purchaser to receive the napkins in the imported form before ultimate use
options.C: The individual restaurant patron who eventually uses one of the napkins during a meal served at the restaurant table
options.D: The napkin manufacturer overseas, since that foreign company produced, packaged, and shipped the paper article for the shipment

question: A recordholder of a trademark notified CBP of infringement concerns and later wants to know how long CBP will generally detain suspect merchandise before either releasing it or proceeding to seizure absent extraordinary circumstances. What best describes CBP's general approach to detention timing in these matters?

options.A: CBP has no authority whatsoever to detain suspect merchandise pending an intellectual property rights investigation at any time or under any circumstances at the border
options.B: CBP may detain suspect merchandise indefinitely with no defined timeframe, notification requirement, or investigative process whatsoever for resolving the matter
options.C: Detention converts into permanent forfeiture shortly after the goods are examined, with limited further process, notice, or opportunity for the importer of record
options.D: CBP applies defined but limited detention periods during which it investigates and notifies parties before deciding whether to release, seize, or otherwise resolve the matter

question: A chocolate maker imports raw cocoa beans from Ghana and processes them in the United States into finished chocolate bars sold to consumers. The importer asks whether the bean sacks must be marked for the retail buyer. Which exception under 19 CFR 134.32 fits this situation best?

options.A: The exception for articles the importer will substantially transform before resale
options.B: The crude substances exception, because unprocessed beans are a crude material
options.C: The exception for articles that would be physically damaged by any marking
options.D: The personal use exception, because the importer uses the beans in its own factory

question: A domestic manufacturer holds a recorded copyright covering original artwork printed on imported textile products. CBP detains a shipment suspected of bearing pirated reproductions of that artwork. What distinguishes this copyright enforcement scenario from an ordinary trademark counterfeit seizure procedurally?

options.A: Copyright enforcement is handled mainly by the United States Copyright Office in Washington, D.C. for these types of claims
options.B: There is little procedural distinction between copyright enforcement and trademark enforcement at the border in practice
options.C: Copyright piracy enforcement centers on unauthorized reproduction of protected creative works rather than use of a confusingly similar source-identifying mark
options.D: Copyright violations can result in the detention of imported merchandise but not in its seizure by CBP at a port of entry

question: An importer's shipment of imported musical instrument strings includes a small quantity of components that are excepted from individual marking under 19 CFR 134.32 because marking would damage the delicate strings. Which additional requirement typically still applies in this situation?

options.D: The exception eliminates any marking requirement permanently for all future shipments of the same product line into the country

question: A broker is training a new entry writer on why Congress requires country of origin marking for imported goods. The trainee asks what interest the marking rule in 19 USC 1304(a) is mainly designed to protect when foreign merchandise enters the United States. Which purpose best describes the foundation of the marking requirement?

options.A: Informing the ultimate purchaser about where the article was made
options.B: Setting the duty rate that applies to each imported article
options.C: Giving CBP a basis to detain merchandise at the port of entry
options.D: Recording the foreign manufacturer in a government database

question: An importer sources raw diamonds mined in Country X, which are then cut, polished, and set into finished jewelry entirely in Country Y before importation into the United States. What is the correct approach to determining the country of origin for marking these finished jewelry pieces?

options.A: Marking origin for jewelry is determined exclusively by where the finished jewelry is ultimately sold at retail to the consumers here in America

question: A broker reviews an entry for imported wristwatches and recalls that watches and watch movements are subject to a special marking statute separate from the general Part 134 rules. What is the primary purpose of this dedicated statutory scheme found in 19 CFR 11.9 and related provisions?

options.B: To exempt imported watches from most country of origin marking requirements under the applicable federal rules

question: CBP detains a shipment of luxury handbags at the port of entry believing the mark is counterfeit. The importer claims the goods are genuine overruns from the licensed factory sold without authorization. What must the importer typically provide to CBP to overcome the detention?

question: A shipment of decorative pins is found to have the country of origin marked, but using an abbreviation that is not commonly recognized by American consumers as referring to the actual exporting country. What compliance concern does this raise under CBP marking guidance?

options.A: Abbreviations are prohibited on country of origin marking even when they are clear and widely recognized by ordinary American purchasers at retail
options.B: The abbreviation may fail the legibility and clarity standard if it does not clearly and unambiguously convey the actual country to an ordinary purchaser
options.C: The concern relates solely to intellectual property recordation rather than to any country of origin marking requirements under the federal marking rules and guidance
options.D: Any abbreviation is automatically acceptable as long as it consists of exactly two capital letters on the marking applied to the goods

question: Merchandise that is the product of the United States, or that has already been entered and duty paid before being brought into the zone, retains its status as such and is not treated as foreign merchandise for zone purposes. What is this status called under 19 CFR 146?

options.A: Domestic status
options.B: Privileged foreign status
options.C: Non-privileged foreign status
options.D: Zone-restricted status

question: A U.S. company owns a federally registered copyright covering a line of imported greeting cards and suspects unauthorized reproductions are entering through a West Coast port. What CBP program allows the copyright owner to alert Customs and request enhanced targeting of these shipments?

question: An importer marks imported furniture with the phrase Product of China even though the wood frame was substantially transformed in Vietnam through complex joinery, finishing, and upholstery work that changed the article's character. What compliance risk does this marking create?

question: After the time allowed for entry expires without any importer coming forward to claim the merchandise, CBP requires the goods be placed into a bonded facility pending eventual public auction. Under 19 CFR 19.1, this facility is properly classified as which warehouse class?

options.B: Class six
options.C: Class one

question: A distributor imports genuine branded cosmetics manufactured abroad by the trademark owner's own foreign affiliate, then sells them in the United States through channels not authorized by the domestic trademark holder. How does CBP typically treat this type of gray-market importation?

question: An importer of canned vegetables from a USMCA country wants to determine the correct origin marking under the Part 102 rules rather than the general substantial transformation test. Which factor is central to the Part 102 tariff shift methodology used for USMCA marking determinations?

question: A trademark owner wants Customs and Border Protection to actively monitor and detain shipments of counterfeit goods bearing its registered mark at the border. What administrative step must the trademark owner first complete with the agency to obtain this enforcement benefit?

question: A textbook publisher imports printed books from Canada that qualify for USMCA preferential tariff treatment under the applicable tariff shift rule. For marking purposes, which regulation governs how the country of origin of these printed books must be determined and labeled?

question: A commodity terminal wants bonded status limited to storing imported grain in dedicated bins, separate from the general cargo warehouse it also operates under a different class designation. What class number under 19 CFR 19.1 must the terminal cite for the grain bin portion?

question: A shipment of aluminum ladders is wholly produced in Malaysia, then shipped through Singapore before arriving in the United States. The marking on the cartons reads Made in Singapore because that was the final port of export. What is the compliance problem?

question: A broker explains to a client that goods from Canada will enter duty free under USMCA, and the client assumes that duty-free status removes the obligation to mark the goods with their country of origin. What should the broker explain about the marking requirement for these imports?

question: A trainee asks the broker to contrast what happens when imported goods are found improperly marked with what happens when imported goods are found to bear counterfeit marks of a recorded trademark. options.B: Improper marking leads to seizure, while counterfeit goods lead only to a marking duty assessment
options.C: Improper marking leads to remarking or a marking duty, while counterfeit goods may be seized

question: Merchandise placed in a zone specifically for the purpose of exportation, destruction, or storage, and which CBP treats as though it had already been exported for most purposes, is admitted under a status that generally forecloses withdrawal for domestic consumption. options.A: Zone-restricted status

question: Bamboo window blinds arrive with slats milled in Indonesia, but the slats were cut, assembled, and finished into complete blinds in Malaysia. Most of the material value comes from Indonesia. A broker must state the country of origin on the marking. Which country applies, and why?

question: An importer brings molded rubber boots from Thailand with the country name formed directly into the rubber of each sole during the molding process. The lettering is readable, sits where a buyer would see it, and cannot rub off. Is this marking method acceptable?

question: While applying the Part 102 marking rules to a USMCA good, a broker must find the specific tariff shift that applies before analyzing the materials. The broker asks where that requirement is stated. How does the chapter describe the location of the applicable tariff shift rule?

question: A broker calendars a client's warehouse entry to ensure the merchandise is withdrawn, exported, or destroyed before the statutory storage deadline expires, after which the goods become subject to CBP's general order procedures. options.A: Five years from the date of importation
options.B: One year from the date the goods entered the warehouse
options.C: Four years, matching the customs bond continuous liability period
options.D: There is no deadline as long as storage fees are paid

question: A trainee asks the broker why certain small hardware items appear on the J-list at 19 CFR 134.33 instead of being marked individually. The broker explains the rationale behind the list. Which reason best explains why these articles are excepted?

question: A broker learns that a client's imported drone parts may infringe a patent held by a domestic manufacturer, and the client asks whether CBP will seize the parts at the port. How does the chapter describe the enforcement path for patent infringement?

question: A broker discovers that an importer falsely marked earbuds with a country that avoided an antidumping duty order. CBP has already assessed the marking duty under 19 USC 1304(f). The client asks whether any other liability may follow. What is the correct answer?

question: A shipment of stainless steel washers arrives in a clear plastic bag that lets a buyer read the country of origin printed on each washer inside. The bag itself carries no separate marking.
