options.C: Transaction value is barred unless CBP first reviews and approves the invoice price the parent charged
options.D: Transaction value remains available only through the fallback method after the other methods are ruled out

question: Merchandise is exported on March 3, the invoice is dated February 26, and the entry is filed on March 15. The invoice is denominated in a foreign currency, and the broker must convert the amount to United States dollars. Under 19 CFR 159.32, which date fixes the exchange rate?

options.A: The invoice date, February 26, is the date the conversion statute uses for the entry
options.B: The entry date, March 15, is the date the conversion statute uses for the shipment
options.C: The date of exportation, March 3, is the date the statute uses
options.D: The earliest of the three dates in the entry file is used for the currency conversion

question: Pentreath Motors hires an engineering firm in the country of export to design a gearbox that the foreign producer will manufacture for export to the United States. The design work is necessary for production and the buyer supplies it free of charge. Under 19 USC 1401a(h)(1), how is that design work treated?

options.A: It is an assist because engineering and design undertaken outside the United States is covered
options.B: It is excluded because design work is a service rather than merchandise supplied for the production run
options.C: It is excluded because the buyer did not perform the design work itself and paid the engineering firm directly
options.D: It is an assist only when the gearbox design is protected by a patent issued in the exporting country

question: In building computed value, the broker must select the profit and general expenses figure. The foreign producer sells comparable merchandise in the country of exportation for shipment to the United States. Under 19 USC 1401a(e), which standard governs that figure?

options.A: The profit the individual producer earned on all of its worldwide sales during the prior year
options.B: The highest profit margin the producer achieved on comparable goods during the last five years
options.C: The amount usually reflected in the same class of goods exported to the United States
options.D: The profit allowed by the exporting country's domestic tax authority for goods of the same class

question: Carlow Manufacturing supplies aluminum sheet to its foreign producer at no charge, and the producer incorporates that sheet into the imported goods. The broker is reviewing whether the sheet is an assist. Under 19 USC 1401a(h)(1), what makes the supplied material an assist?

options.A: The buyer supplied it free of charge for use in producing the imported merchandise
options.B: The producer paid nothing at any point for the material actually used to make the imported goods
options.C: The material was supplied by the buyer rather than purchased by the foreign producer for the production run
options.D: The material represents more than half of the finished article value after the goods are fully assembled

question: CBP computes deductive value from a United States resale price and must subtract the importer's usual return on goods of the same class or kind. The broker is checking the allowable deduction. Under 19 USC 1401a(d), which deduction covers that return?

options.A: The producer's profit and general expenses in the country where the imported goods were made
options.B: The buyer's selling commission paid to the foreign seller's agent for negotiating the purchase
options.C: The international freight and insurance paid before the goods arrived at the United States port
options.D: The usual commission or the usual profit and general expenses for that class of goods

question: Wrenfield Supply buys goods for $30,000.00 on an FOB basis and separately pays $2,400.00 for ocean freight and $600.00 for insurance, each itemized on the invoice and the entry documents. The broker is computing transaction value. Under 19 USC 1401a(b), how are those two charges treated?

options.A: Both charges are excluded because separately itemized international freight and insurance is not dutiable
options.B: Both charges are added because they move the imported goods into the United States for the buyer's own use
options.C: Only the insurance is added because ocean freight is treated as a seller cost under this sale term for the shipment
options.D: Only the freight is added because insurance is treated as a service charge for the purchaser's benefit under the sale

question: After documenting a price that recovers the seller's full cost plus profit consistent with the firm's overall profit on goods of the same class or kind, the importer does not attempt the test values comparison. Under 19 USC 1401a, may transaction value still be used?

options.A: No, because both related party tests must be satisfied together before transaction value can be used
options.B: No, because the test values comparison is the primary statutory test and is run first
options.C: Yes, but only if CBP waives the circumstances of the sale test after reviewing the importer's cost records
options.D: Yes, because only one of the two related party tests needs to be satisfied

question: Camborne Supply Group buys from a foreign affiliate, and CBP finds the affiliate set the invoice price below what unrelated buyers pay for comparable goods. The importer offers no evidence that the relationship did not affect the price. Under 19 USC 1401a(b)(2), what is the result?

options.A: Transaction value is unavailable because the relationship influenced the price
options.B: Transaction value applies because a sale and an invoice price exist for the imported merchandise
options.C: Transaction value applies if the affiliate is a separate legal entity that keeps its own accounting records
options.D: Transaction value is unavailable only after CBP issues a penalty notice covering the related party transaction

question: A related party importer cannot fully satisfy the circumstances of the sale test, so the broker turns to the test values comparison. Under 19 USC 1401a, which comparisons may the importer use to show the price closely approximates an acceptable value?

options.A: The price the seller charged its largest unrelated customer for comparable goods in the same calendar year period
options.B: The listed price in the exporting country's domestic wholesale catalog for goods of that same class of merchandise
options.C: Identical or similar merchandise values for unrelated buyers, including transaction, deductive, or computed value
options.D: The highest price the seller obtained from a different customer for merchandise of the same class during that year

question: Selby Interiors buys imported glassware for $28,000.00 and must pay $2,000.00 directly to an unrelated patent holder as a condition of the sale, for technology embodied in the glassware. The seller does not receive the payment. Under 19 USC 1401a(b)(1), how is the payment treated?

options.A: It is excluded because the seller does not receive the royalty payment and has no interest in the patent
options.B: It is excluded because the licensor and the seller are separate companies with no ownership relationship
options.C: It is added only if the seller guarantees the technology works and the buyer relies on that guarantee
options.D: It is added because royalties paid directly or indirectly as a condition of sale count

question: Thornbury Trading pays $18,000.00 for imported lamps and a separate $900.00 fee to an agent who represents the foreign seller, negotiates the sale on the seller's behalf, and takes no risk in the transaction. Under 19 USC 1401a(b)(1), how is the $900.00 fee treated?

options.A: It is excluded as a buying commission because the buyer paid the fee to the seller's agent at entry
options.B: It is added as a selling commission because the agent represents the seller
options.C: It is excluded because the commission fee is stated separately from the invoice price of the lamps
options.D: It is added only if the buyer directed the agent's daily work and set the terms of the negotiation

question: Dunmore Foods pays its foreign seller $3,000.00 for the right to distribute the seller's other product lines in the United States. The payment is not connected to the imported merchandise and is not a condition of buying it. Under 19 USC 1401a(b)(1), how is that payment treated?

options.A: It is added because every payment made to the foreign seller raises the dutiable value of the goods
options.B: It is added because the buyer benefits from the distribution rights the seller granted in the agreement
options.C: It is excluded because a royalty for resale or distribution rights alone is not added
options.D: It is excluded only if the seller grants the distribution rights in a separate written agreement filed with CBP

question: Fairwick Distributors imports goods for which no statutory method can be applied, and CBP is considering a fallback valuation. A customs officer proposes a fixed minimum value per unit adopted from a foreign government schedule. Under 19 USC 1401a(f), is that approach permitted?

options.A: No, because minimum values are expressly prohibited under the fallback method
options.B: Yes, because adopting a fixed minimum value from the foreign government schedule supplies a predictable dutiable figure
options.C: Yes, because the importer may agree to a fixed value before liquidation and thereby supply the missing appraised value
options.D: No, because fallback may rely only on the transaction value of identical or similar merchandise sold for export to the United States

question: Marlowe Beverages imports sparkling water under a contract that limits the buyer to reselling the goods within three named western states. A price is stated, and no other condition affects the sale. Under 19 USC 1401a(b)(2), does the geographic limit disqualify transaction value?

options.A: Yes, because any limit placed on the resale territory of the imported goods defeats transaction value for the sale
options.B: No, because a restriction on the geographic area of resale does not disqualify transaction value
options.C: Yes, unless the importer files a separate territorial disclosure with the port director before the entry is liquidated
options.D: No, because territorial limits apply only to consigned merchandise that remains under the foreign seller's ownership

question: Hartwell Ceramics supplies its foreign producer, free of charge, with a chemical catalyst that is consumed during firing and never appears in the finished tile. The catalyst is necessary to produce the imported goods. Under 19 USC 1401a(h)(1), is the catalyst an assist?

options.A: No, because the catalyst is consumed during the firing process and is not physically incorporated in the finished tile
options.B: No, because a consumed item is treated as a packing supply rather than as a dutiable assist under the statute
options.C: Yes, but only if the producer pays part of the catalyst cost and later passes that cost to the buyer
options.D: Yes, because merchandise consumed in producing the imported goods is an assist

question: Roydon Cycles ships free of charge to its foreign assembler a batch of bicycle derailleurs that the assembler attaches to bicycles sold to Roydon. The derailleurs are incorporated into the finished goods. Under 19 USC 1401a(h)(1), how is that supply treated?

options.A: As a packing cost because the parts travel with the finished goods to the buyer in the shipment
options.B: As a buying commission because the importer supplied the parts to the assembler free of charge
options.C: As an assist because components and parts incorporated in the goods are covered
options.D: As a post-importation charge because assembly of the finished bicycles occurs after entry in the United States

question: Selby Interiors pays $24,000.00 for imported textiles and a separate $1,200.00 fee to its own agent in the country of export. The agent negotiated solely for Selby, bore its own risk, and held no stake in the seller's profit. Under 19 USC 1401a(b)(1), how is the fee treated?

options.A: It is added because commissions paid by the buyer raise dutiable value
options.B: It is added unless the agent is a national of the exporting country
options.C: It is excluded only if the seller reimburses the fee to the buyer
options.D: It is excluded because the fee is a bona fide buying commission

question: A broker explains the three duty structures to a client importing bottled juice. The client wants to know which structure produces a charge that depends on the quantity of merchandise rather than on the value of the shipment as a percentage. Which structure is that?

options.A: A specific duty, which is a flat amount per unit of quantity
options.B: An ad valorem duty, which is a percentage of the appraised value
options.C: A compound duty, which combines a percentage with a flat amount
options.D: A fixed duty, which is set once for the importer's annual entries

question: Lansdowne Toolworks receives an invoice that separately lists $18,000.00 for the merchandise and $2,160.00 for United States import duties advanced by the seller at entry. The broker is establishing transaction value for the shipment. Under 19 USC 1401a(b), how is the $2,160.00 treated?

options.A: It is added because the seller advanced the duty payment on behalf of the buyer at the time of entry
options.B: It is added because the buyer ultimately bears the duty cost as part of the purchase arrangement
options.C: It is excluded because United States import duties are not part of dutiable value
options.D: It is excluded only when CBP has already collected the duty from the seller of the imported merchandise

question: Bexley Home Imports buys furniture for $40,000.00 and, at the seller's direction, separately pays $3,500.00 to a lender to clear a debt the seller owed that lender. The broker is determining the price actually paid or payable. Under 19 USC 1401a(b), how is the $3,500.00 payment treated?

options.A: It is excluded because the buyer paid a third party rather than the foreign seller itself for the debt
options.B: It is excluded because the payment is labeled a loan settlement between the buyer and the lender
options.C: It is added only if the lender is related to the foreign seller and the buyer knew of the relationship
options.D: It is added to the price as an indirect payment for the seller's benefit

question: Nicolet Instruments enters 4,500 kilograms of scientific glassware with a transaction value of $60,000.00. The applicable tariff line carries a specific duty of 4.0 cents per kilogram of entered quantity and no ad valorem component. What duty is owed on this entry?

options.A: $2,400.00, the duty computed as a percentage of the entered value
options.B: $180.00, the duty computed as a flat amount per entered kilogram
options.C: $90.00, the duty computed on half of the entered kilograms
options.D: $240.00, the duty computed on six thousand entered kilograms

question: Ilkley Machine Works buys imported presses at a stated price, but the contract also requires the buyer to provide the seller an unspecified quantity of future technical support with no measurable value. No reliable figure for that consideration exists. Under 19 USC 1401a(b)(2), what is the effect on transaction value?

options.A: Transaction value remains available because the invoice price is clearly stated for the imported presses
options.B: Transaction value remains available because the parties are unrelated and the invoice reflects the full price
options.C: Transaction value fails only if CBP proves the technical support had a real value at the time of sale
options.D: Transaction value fails because the sale is subject to a condition of undetermined value

question: Adair Provisions enters 3,000 kilograms of processed fruit with a transaction value of $15,000.00. The tariff line carries a compound rate of 2.5 cents per kilogram plus 2.0 percent ad valorem. What is the total duty owed for this entry?

options.A: $300.00, the ad valorem component computed on the appraised value alone
options.B: $375.00, the specific component plus the ad valorem component together
options.C: $75.00, the specific component computed on the entered kilograms alone
options.D: $450.00, the sum of the specific component and a 2.5 percent rate

question: Ridgeway Outfitters imports camping gear that cannot be valued under any of the first five methods. A consultant recommends appraising the goods using the price of comparable merchandise produced and sold in the United States. Under 19 USC 1401a(f), what is the correct treatment of that recommendation?

options.A: It is proper because values for comparable merchandise produced and sold in the United States reflect current market conditions
options.B: It is proper when the imported merchandise is later sold at the same retail price point in the United States
options.C: It is prohibited because the exporting country's home market price is preferred over any other measure of value
options.D: It is prohibited because the domestic selling price of United States goods cannot be used

question: The president of a United States importer also serves as a director of the foreign company that manufactures the goods it buys. Does that overlapping role make the two companies related parties under the statutory categories at 19 USC 1401a(g)?

options.A: They are related, because officers or directors of one another's businesses are listed
options.B: They are related, because directors are treated as employees of both companies, since a director serves each business
options.C: They are not related, because a directorship is not an ownership interest, since no shares change hands
options.D: They are not related, because the two companies are separately incorporated, since each stands as its own legal person

question: Two foreign producers in the same country supply candidate merchandise for comparison. One producer's goods differ in quality and reputation from the imported goods. The broker is selecting a secondary appraisement method. Under 19 USC 1401a, what does identical merchandise require?

options.A: Merchandise with like characteristics and component materials made in a different country
options.B: Merchandise that is commercially interchangeable and performs the same functions
options.C: Merchandise the same in all respects, produced in the same foreign country
options.D: Merchandise sold in the exporting country's domestic market at wholesale prices

question: A broker cannot use transaction value of the imported merchandise or of identical merchandise, and now compares goods with like characteristics made in the same country by a different producer. The goods serve the same uses and buyers treat them as substitutes. Under 19 USC 1401a, which standard applies to this comparison?

options.A: Merchandise the same in all respects, including physical characteristics and quality, which describes identical goods
options.B: Merchandise produced in another country by a producer under common ownership, which describes related-party goods
options.C: Merchandise valued from the price at which it resells in the United States, which describes deductive value
options.D: Merchandise with like characteristics and materials, same country, commercially interchangeable

question: Two brothers own the importing company and the foreign manufacturing company that will supply it. The broker reviews the relationship before choosing an appraisement method for the first shipment of camping stoves. Are the two companies related parties under 19 USC 1401a(g)?

options.A: They are related, because family members are a listed category of related parties
options.B: They are related only if one brother owns five percent of the other's company
options.C: They are not related, because the two companies were formed separately
options.D: They are not related, because only business ties create a related-party relationship

question: For imported industrial vacuum pumps, the foreign producer reports materials and fabrication of $28,000.00 and profit and general expenses of $7,000.00. A buyer-supplied assist not reflected in those figures is worth $3,000.00, and packing costs are $1,000.00. What is the computed value?

options.A: $35,000.00, the materials and fabrication plus the profit and general expenses
options.B: $36,000.00, the materials, fabrication, profit, and packing costs only
options.C: $38,000.00, the materials, fabrication, profit, and the assist only
options.D: $39,000.00, the materials, fabrication, profit, assist, and packing together

question: Harbor Point Trading imports cordless drills that embody a patented chuck. The buyer must pay $3.00 per drill to an unrelated patent holder as a condition of buying the drills from the foreign seller. How does that payment affect transaction value?

options.A: It is added, because a condition-of-sale royalty paid indirectly is dutiable
options.B: It is excluded, because the patent holder is not the seller of the drills
options.C: It is excluded, because the buyer paid the patent holder rather than the seller
options.D: It is added, because payments tied to patented goods are packing costs

question: A foreign producer supplies cost data for imported bicycle helmets so that computed value can be established, and the producer wants the profit element to reflect its highest margin on a premium product line. How is the profit element of computed value measured?

options.A: The producer's actual profit on the specific shipment being appraised at the time, since that margin is known
options.B: The profit and general expenses usually reflected in sales of that class of goods
options.C: The profit the importer earns when the helmets are resold in the United States, since that is the importer's return
options.D: The highest profit margin the producer obtains on any of its export products, since the best margin would be used

question: A broker computes deductive value for imported marble countertops. The goods sold to unrelated buyers in the greatest aggregate quantity for $48,000.00. Usual profit and general expenses are $9,600.00, post-importation freight and insurance are $1,800.00, and customs duties are $2,700.00. What is the deductive value?

options.A: $48,000.00, the resale price before any of the deductions are taken, since nothing has been subtracted yet
options.B: $36,600.00, the resale price less profit, general expenses, and freight, but not the duties
options.C: $35,700.00, the resale price less profit, general expenses, and duties, but not the freight
options.D: $33,900.00, the resale price less profit, general expenses, freight, and duties

question: A broker reviews a license agreement connected to imported digital scales. The importer pays a per-unit royalty to the seller for a patented weighing mechanism built into the goods, and the seller will not complete the sale without the royalty. What two conditions make the royalty dutiable?

options.A: The royalty relates to the imported merchandise and payment is a condition of the sale
options.B: The royalty is paid after importation and is documented in the license agreement, since the agreement links it to the goods
options.C: The royalty is a percentage of the resale price and is paid to the seller, since a resale-based payment is dutiable
options.D: The royalty is paid in the same currency as the merchandise invoice price, since that ties the payment to the sale

question: A broker builds a deductive value analysis for imported patio umbrellas and must start from the sale price the statute designates. The goods sold in the United States at or about the time of importation in a range of quantities and prices. Which unit price is the correct starting measure?

options.A: The highest unit price obtained for any single umbrella sold in the United States
options.B: The average unit price across all umbrellas the importer sold that season
options.C: The unit price the importer would charge in a future catalog listing
options.D: The unit price at which the greatest aggregate quantity of the goods sold

question: Silver Creek Tools imports bench grinders. The importer supplied the producer a molding tool free of charge, and the seller's invoice separately states a $6,000.00 tooling charge, which the buyer paid as part of the price. What addition does the broker make?

options.A: No further addition is made, because the tooling is already included in the price
options.B: The $6,000.00 is added again, because assists are counted apart from the invoice, since the charge is listed separately
options.C: The $6,000.00 is added again, because a tooling charge is a separate service, since the work was done for the buyer
options.D: No addition is made, because tools supplied by a buyer are not dutiable, since the tool remains the buyer's property

question: Appraisement of imported air compressors uses deductive value. The goods sold to unrelated buyers in the greatest aggregate quantity for $32,000.00, and the importer's usual profit and general expenses for goods of the same class or kind equal $6,400.00. What is the deductive value?

options.A: $32,000.00, the resale price obtained in the greatest aggregate quantity
options.B: $30,400.00, the resale price less five percent of value for customs duties
options.C: $25,600.00, the resale price less the usual profit and general expenses
options.D: $38,400.00, the resale price plus the usual profit and general expenses

question: An importer of marine propellers pays a United States engineering firm $25,000.00 to develop designs that the foreign producer uses. The work was performed entirely in the United States, and the buyer supplied the results free of charge. How is that design cost treated?

options.A: It is excluded, because engineering work performed in the United States is not an assist
options.B: It is added, because design work supplied free of charge is an assist, since the buyer supplied the design
options.C: It is added, because the buyer paid for work used in producing the goods, as buyer-supplied work
options.D: It is excluded, because the design was not invoiced to the foreign producer as a separate item

question: Ashwood Audio imports 500 turntables at $80.00 each, for an invoice price of $40,000.00. As a condition of the sale, the buyer must pay a $4.00 per unit royalty for a patented tonearm used in the goods, which is not reflected in the unit price. What is the transaction value?

options.A: $40,000.00, the invoice price shown for the imported turntables
options.B: $42,000.00, the invoice price plus the per-unit royalty on the goods
options.C: $44,000.00, the invoice price plus a flat royalty of $4,000.00 per license
options.D: $38,000.00, the invoice price less the royalty paid to the licensor

question: Blue Ridge Saddlery imports leather work boots from an unrelated manufacturer. The buyer pays a $2,000.00 fee to an agent who represents the seller, finds the buyer, and is paid for bringing about the sale. How does that fee affect transaction value?

options.A: It is added as a selling commission because the agent represents the seller
options.B: It is excluded as a buying commission because the buyer paid the fee directly to the agent
options.C: It is added as an assist because the agent helped produce the boots, since the buyer supplied the work
options.D: It is excluded because commissions paid by a buyer sit outside the price, since a buyer's payment is not part of it

question: Trelane Outdoor imports hiking boots. The buyer supplied the producer a cutting die valued at $20,000.00 at reduced cost, and the producer reimbursed $7,500.00 toward that die. The die is used only for these boots and is fully apportioned. What amount is added as an assist?

options.A: $20,000.00 is added, because the die's full value was supplied to the producer, without deduction
options.B: $12,500.00 is added, because the assist is valued net of the producer's payment
options.C: $7,500.00 is added, because only the producer's own contribution is dutiable, since that is what he paid
options.D: Nothing is added, because the producer shared the cost of the cutting die, since he paid part of it

question: Mowbray Lighting imports 800 pendant lamps at $22.00 per lamp, for an invoice price of $17,600.00. The buyer also paid $900.00 for the cartons and $400.00 for the labor used to pack the lamps for export. No other amounts apply to this shipment. What is the transaction value?

options.A: $18,900.00, the invoice price plus the buyer-paid packing costs
options.B: $17,600.00, the invoice price shown by the foreign seller
options.C: $18,500.00, the invoice price plus the cost of the cartons alone
options.D: $19,300.00, the invoice price plus packing and a selling commission

question: Adair Provisions imports commercial food slicers. The buyer hired an engineering studio in the producer's country to design the slicing mechanism, paid $18,000.00 for that work, and provided the drawings to the producer free of charge. How is that design cost treated?

options.A: The design cost is excluded because the buyer did not supply materials or parts
options.B: The design cost is added as an assist because the work was undertaken abroad
options.C: The design cost is added as a selling commission paid by the buyer
options.D: The design cost is excluded because engineering work is treated as overhead

question: A United States importer owns six percent of the voting stock of the foreign producer that supplies its vinyl flooring, and the same foreign producer owns six percent of the importer's voting stock. Are the parties related for valuation purposes?

options.A: They are not related, because neither party holds a controlling interest
options.B: They are not related, because the cross holdings fall below ten percent
options.C: They are related, because each owns five percent or more of the other's stock
options.D: They are related only if the same person controls both of the companies

question: An importer buys precision measuring instruments from a foreign producer at a heavily reduced price. The contract requires the importer to destroy the instruments after a single use and bars any resale, a restriction bearing directly on what the goods are worth. Can transaction value be used?

options.A: Transaction value remains available, because the parties agreed to the price in writing, since the agreed price fixes value
options.B: Transaction value remains available, because the buyer accepted the restriction, since acceptance shows the price is reliable
options.C: Transaction value is not available, because the restriction substantially affects value
options.D: Transaction value is not available, because the price was set below the market, since that level cannot support a value

question: Harbor Point Trading buys industrial pumps from an unrelated foreign seller for $40,000.00. Separately, and at the seller's request, the buyer pays $5,000.00 to a steel supplier to settle a debt the seller owed that supplier for metal used in the pumps. Which amount is part of the price actually paid or payable?

options.A: $45,000.00, because the payment to the supplier is an indirect payment to the seller
options.B: $40,000.00, because the buyer sent the extra funds to a supplier outside the sale of the pumps
options.C: $40,000.00, because the supplier is not a party to the sale of the pumps themselves
options.D: $45,000.00, because the extra payment settles a debt owed by the seller to the supplier

question: Winterbourne Home imports 400 stoneware planters at $35.00 each, for an invoice price of $14,000.00. The buyer pays a $700.00 commission to an agent who represents the seller, and separately pays $600.00 in itemized ocean freight. What is the transaction value of this shipment?

options.A: $15,300.00, the invoice price plus the commission and the freight
options.B: $14,000.00, the invoice price shown on the seller's commercial invoice
options.C: $14,600.00, the invoice price plus the itemized ocean freight charge
options.D: $14,700.00, the invoice price plus the selling commission

question: A foreign manufacturer's export manager negotiates a sale of aluminum ladders to a United States importer and charges a three percent fee. The export manager reports to the manufacturer and is paid only when the manufacturer's goods sell. How should this fee be classified?

options.A: A buying commission, because the importer paid the fee to the export manager
options.B: A selling commission, because the agent serves the seller's interests
options.C: A packing cost, because the fee is tied to preparing the goods for shipment
options.D: An assist, because the export manager contributed to producing the ladders

question: CBP is considering a fallback appraisement for a shipment of imported ceramic tile and reviewing the candidate figures with the broker of record. Which of the four candidate figures is forbidden as a basis for that fallback appraisement under the statute?

options.A: The domestic selling price of merchandise produced in the United States
options.B: The unit price at which the greatest aggregate quantity is sold in the United States
options.C: The price actually paid or payable for the goods in the export sale
options.D: The cost of materials and fabrication recorded in the producer's accounts

question: Fairhaven Optics imports digital cameras for $60,000.00 from an unrelated manufacturer. At the seller's direction and at its insistence, the buyer also sends $4,000.00 to a design firm the seller had engaged. How is that $4,000.00 payment treated for transaction value purposes?

options.A: The $4,000.00 is excluded because it did not go to the seller's bank account
options.B: The $4,000.00 is included because it was paid for the seller's benefit
options.C: The $4,000.00 is excluded because design services are not merchandise
options.D: The $4,000.00 is included as a packing cost borne by the buyer of the cameras

question: A foreign seller's invoice for imported binoculars shows a $52,000.00 merchandise price plus a $3,000.00 charge described as a documentation fee. The seller would not release the shipment unless the extra charge was paid with the price. What amount is dutiable?

options.A: $52,000.00, because a documentation fee is a service cost rather than merchandise value
options.B: $55,000.00, because the fee is an assist supplied to the foreign producer, as an assist
options.C: $52,000.00, because only the merchandise price stated on the invoice can be dutiable
options.D: $55,000.00, because the total payment to the seller forms the price actually paid

question: A broker is briefing a new importer on the legal basis for appraising imported merchandise. The broker explains that the current appraisement system replaced the older export value and foreign value standards with a framework built around an actual commercial transaction. Which statute supplies that framework?

options.A: The Trade Agreements Act of 1979, codified at 19 USC 1401a
options.B: The Tariff Act of 1930 alone, before any later statutory amendment
options.C: The Customs Modernization Act, standing alone as the valuation statute
options.D: The Harmonized Tariff Schedule, which sets value as well as duty rates
