Beacon Toy Distributors pays $51,500.00, the price actually paid or payable, for aluminum cookware, and separately pays a bona fide buying commission of $880.00 to its own agent in the country of export, who negotiated the purchase solely on Beacon Toy Distributors's behalf. What is the transaction value?

Redwood Electronics LLC purchases ceramic dinnerware for $19,750.00, the price actually paid or payable, on an FOB basis. The buyer separately paid $890.00 in packing costs incurred to prepare the merchandise for export, which are not already included in the invoice price. What is the transaction value?

Redwood Electronics LLC imports woven area rugs from an unrelated foreign manufacturer for $39,250.00, the price actually paid. The importer supplied tooling worth $2,900.00 free of charge to the manufacturer for use in producing the goods. What is the transaction value of this shipment under 19 USC 1401a?

Ashford Textiles Inc. pays $51,500.00, the price actually paid or payable, for ceramic dinnerware, plus a separate selling commission of $1,050.00 paid to an agent who represents the foreign seller and negotiated the sale on the seller's behalf. What is the transaction value?

Ashford Textiles Inc. imports steel fasteners from an unrelated foreign manufacturer for $39,250.00, the price actually paid. The importer supplied tooling worth $900.00 free of charge to the manufacturer for use in producing the goods. What is the transaction value of this shipment under 19 USC 1401a?

Palmetto Furniture Co. pays $28,900.00, the price actually paid or payable, for printed circuit assemblies, plus a separate selling commission of $880.00 paid to an agent who represents the foreign seller and negotiated the sale on the seller's behalf. What is the transaction value?

An importer of drinkware in Oregon receives a reusable coffee mug with a permanently affixed silicone sleeve grip molded directly onto the mug's exterior during manufacturing, and the sleeve cannot be detached. How should this article be classified for tariff purposes?

options.A: As a single composite article under GRI 1, since the sleeve is permanently integrated during manufacture
options.B: As two separate articles, requiring separate entries for the ceramic mug and the silicone molded sleeve, with each part carrying its own duty rate
options.C: Under GRI 3(c) as an automatic tiebreaker between the silicone and ceramic headings in the schedule
options.D: Under Chapter 98 as an article that was repaired or altered abroad and then returned to the country

question: Coastal Hardware Traders purchases aluminum cookware for $48,200.00, the price actually paid or payable, on an FOB basis. The buyer separately paid $720.00 in packing costs incurred to prepare the merchandise for export, which are not already included in the invoice price. What is the transaction value?

Ashford Textiles Inc. imports ceramic dinnerware from an unrelated foreign manufacturer for $52,000.00, the price actually paid. The importer supplied tooling worth $1,200.00 free of charge to the manufacturer for use in producing the goods. What is the transaction value of this shipment under 19 USC 1401a?

In Houston, an importer's customs broker is advising a manufacturer that asks whether a binding ruling can be requested for merchandise that will be imported by multiple different importers of record, with the manufacturer seeking guidance to share with its customers. What is the general answer?

options.A: Manufacturers are barred from participating in the binding ruling process, since only importers of record may file a request with CBP
options.B: A ruling request can generally be filed by a party such as a manufacturer, and the resulting ruling addresses the described merchandise
options.C: A separate identical ruling request must be filed by every downstream customer individually, since no ruling travels with the goods to other buyers
options.D: Only the actual importer of record for a specific single shipment may request a ruling, and no other party may participate in the request

question: Lakeside Ceramics imports injection molded auto trim from an unrelated foreign manufacturer for $16,800.00, the price actually paid. The importer supplied tooling worth $3,400.00 free of charge to the manufacturer for use in producing the goods. What is the transaction value of this shipment under 19 USC 1401a?

A broker's client imports a reusable shopping cart liner made of woven fabric with reinforced plastic corner clips permanently attached during manufacturing. When the liner and clips are made of clearly different materials serving different functions, what classification analysis applies here?

options.A: Automatic classification under whichever heading names the plastic corner clips specifically in the schedule for the product
options.B: GRI 3(b) essential character analysis, likely favoring the fabric providing the article's primary structure and use
options.C: Separate classification of the plastic clips and the woven fabric under two distinct entries at the port
options.D: GRI 5(a), treating the plastic corner clips as a specially shaped container that holds the fabric liner, so the case rule governs

question: Vantage Kitchenware imports aluminum cookware from an unrelated foreign manufacturer for $16,800.00, the price actually paid. The importer supplied tooling worth $1,200.00 free of charge to the manufacturer for use in producing the goods. What is the transaction value of this shipment under 19 USC 1401a?

In Newark, an importer's trade compliance analyst is preparing a binding ruling request for an importer of footwear and must decide whether to describe the material composition using precise percentages by weight of each textile and rubber component. What is the correct approach?

options.A: Material composition is irrelevant to the classification of footwear under the HTSUS schedule
options.B: Provide precise material composition and percentages, since this often directly affects classification
options.C: General descriptions such as mostly textile are sufficient for footwear rulings at the port of entry
options.D: Only the country of manufacture needs to be specified in a ruling request for the footwear, since footwear duty rates turn on the material used

question: In Baltimore, a senior customs broker is advising an importer who asks whether a binding ruling remains valid indefinitely if the underlying HTSUS heading language is later amended by statute, even though CBP has not separately revoked the ruling. What is the correct answer?

options.A: A ruling may no longer be valid if the underlying legal text it relied upon has since changed
options.B: A ruling remains permanently binding on CBP despite any later statutory changes to the tariff
options.C: Only CBP headquarters rulings are affected by statutory amendments, and not rulings issued by a port
options.D: Statutory amendments to the HTSUS do not affect binding rulings that were previously issued by CBP

question: An importer brings in a protective chest guard, a piece of sporting equipment, that includes small removable foam pads inserted into fixed fabric pockets sewn into the guard's shell. How should the removable foam pads be treated relative to the guard?

options.A: Classified separately under the general heading for foam articles, without regard to the function they perform in the guard
options.B: Classified together with the guard as a single composite article, since they are designed and sold as one functional unit
options.C: Classified under GRI 5(a) as a specially fitted container that holds the foam in the chest guard, so the case rule controls
options.D: Excluded from the entry as duty-free replaceable components, since the pads are sold as spares for the guard

question: A travel goods importer brings in a pillow with a permanently attached elastic strap designed to secure it to a suitcase handle during travel, and the strap cannot be removed. How should this integrated strap feature be treated for classification purposes?

options.A: As a separately classifiable article under the general heading for elastic textile straps of this kind
options.B: Under GRI 2(a), treating the elastic strap as an unfinished version of the pillow itself in the set
options.C: As duty-free promotional hardware that must be excluded from the entered value of the entire shipment, and the strap is entered as part of the pillow
options.D: As part of the single composite pillow article, since it is permanently integrated and functionally related

question: In Miami, a senior customs broker is advising an importer who wants to know what happens to pending entries already filed under a particular classification if CBP later issues a binding ruling that classifies the same merchandise differently. What is generally true regarding these pending entries?

options.A: Pending entries are unaffected by a ruling that CBP issues later on the same goods, whatever the effective date, and the entries stand as filed
options.B: All previously filed entries are automatically and retroactively voided the moment a new ruling on the goods issues from CBP at headquarters
options.C: The new ruling generally governs future entries, while treatment of already filed entries depends on the ruling's stated effective date
options.D: The importer may choose whichever of the two classifications produces a lower duty liability on the entries already filed

question: In Long Beach, a senior customs broker is classifying a shipment for an outdoor gear importer where a tent, ground stakes, and a carrying bag are packaged together, all designed and sold as one coordinated camping shelter system. Which classification result follows under GRI 3(b)?

options.A: Classification as a set according to the tent, likely giving the article essential character
options.B: Classification of each item separately under its own distinct heading in the schedule, with the duty rate applied to each one
options.C: Classification solely by the carrying bag, as the outermost component of the set, and the bag then carries the entry for the set
options.D: Classification under GRI 2(a) as an unfinished tent structure awaiting its stakes

question: An importer received a binding ruling covering merchandise entered through one port and now plans to bring identical merchandise through a different port of entry. Can the earlier ruling be relied upon for the new entries at that other port?

options.A: Each port maintains its own separate binding ruling system that is unrelated to the systems at other ports, even for identical goods
options.B: A binding ruling generally applies to the described merchandise regardless of the specific port of entry used
options.C: A binding ruling is valid only at the exact port where the ruling request was originally filed by the importer
options.D: A new ruling request must be filed separately for every individual port of entry that will handle the goods

question: An importer is deciding whether to seek a binding ruling for a routine, well established commodity that has been classified consistently under the same heading by the importer and industry for many years without dispute. What consideration is most relevant to this decision?

options.A: Whether the commodity happens to begin with a letter early in the alphabet of the schedule
options.B: Whether the importer's broker license was issued within the past five years by the agency, and the vintage of the license settles the question
options.C: Whether meaningful classification uncertainty or risk actually exists for this particular commodity
options.D: Whether the importer has previously submitted any ruling request on any product to CBP

question: A broker's client imports a reusable water bottle with a built-in fruit infuser basket, both permanently integrated into one molded plastic structure that functions as a single drinking vessel and is sold as one finished product. How should the broker classify this article?

options.A: As two separate articles, requiring separate entries for the water bottle and the infuser basket
options.B: As a single composite drinking vessel article under GRI 1, given the integrated structure
options.C: Under GRI 5(a), treating the fruit infuser basket as a specially fitted container in the bottle
options.D: Under Chapter 98 as an article that was previously exported from the country and returned

question: In Miami, an importer's customs broker is preparing a ruling request for an importer and wants to know whether CBP will consider commercial documents such as purchase orders and technical specification sheets as part of the classification analysis. What is the general practice?

options.A: CBP generally considers relevant commercial and technical documentation submitted to support the request
options.B: CBP is legally barred from reviewing any commercial documents that accompany a ruling request for the goods
options.C: Only government issued certificates of origin may be submitted with a request for a ruling on the goods
options.D: Commercial documents may be submitted only after the ruling on the merchandise has already been issued

question: In Seattle, a senior customs broker is classifying a kitchen appliance package for an importer where a food processor base unit arrives with several interchangeable cutting and blending attachments, all sold together, and the base unit provides the motor. What controls under GRI 3(b)?

options.A: The attachments collectively, since there are more attachment pieces than base units
options.B: The base unit, since it houses the motor and primary function of the appliance
options.C: Whichever attachment was manufactured in a different country from the base unit
options.D: The retail box, since it is the largest physical component of the shipment

question: In Houston, a senior customs broker is answering a client's request to explain the practical difference between requesting a binding ruling and relying on informal advice from a CBP import specialist during a phone call. What is the key distinction?

options.A: Both an informal phone call and a formal binding ruling carry identical legal weight for the entry
options.B: A binding ruling requires prior approval from the informal phone advice given by the import specialist
options.C: Phone advice from an import specialist is more current than a written ruling on the same product
options.D: Only a formal binding ruling carries legal reliability an importer can affirmatively depend upon

question: In Norfolk, a customs broker is classifying specialized medical devices for an importer who is unsure whether a component qualifies under a use provision requiring the article's principal use or under an eo nomine provision naming the device directly. What distinguishes these two provision types?

options.A: An eo nomine provision names the article directly, while a use provision requires an inquiry into actual principal use
options.B: A use provision yields a lower duty rate than an eo nomine provision for the same medical device at entry, and that is the only difference between the two
options.C: Eo nomine provisions apply only to articles that are imported in a disassembled condition at the port
options.D: There is no legal distinction between an eo nomine provision and a use provision in the tariff schedule

question: An importer brings in jewelry made primarily of a base metal alloy but plated with a thin layer of precious metal for appearance, and a chapter note addresses how plated articles of this kind should be classified. What role does this note play in the classification?

options.A: It is purely decorative commentary in the chapter with no bearing on the correct heading for the goods
options.B: It applies only when the plating exceeds fifty percent of the total weight of the plated article
options.C: It is superseded by GRI 3(b) essential character analysis in every case involving plated goods
options.D: It supplies binding classification guidance for plated articles that must be applied under GRI 1

question: An imported article is a stroller that converts into a car seat carrier through a simple mechanism, marketed and sold as one combined product performing two related child transportation functions. Which classification approach applies when GRI 1 does not resolve the choice between competing headings?

options.A: GRI 5(b), treating the conversion mechanism as ordinary packing material for the stroller, and the mechanism then follows the stroller
options.B: GRI 3(b) essential character analysis, examining which function dominates the combined article
options.C: Automatic classification under whichever of the two headings appears first in numerical order
options.D: Classification under Chapter 98 as a repaired or altered article returned to the country

question: While classifying an imported article, a broker identifies a chapter note stating that goods described in that note are to be classified there whether or not they are also described in a heading elsewhere in the schedule. What effect does this kind of note have?

options.A: It has no legal effect beyond providing general informational background for the classification decision
options.B: It is automatically superseded by any more specific eo nomine heading found elsewhere in the schedule
options.C: It gives the note's chapter priority classification even over an otherwise applicable heading elsewhere
options.D: It applies only if the importer specifically elects to use that chapter on the entry summary at entry, and the note binds the entry in that situation

question: An importer that obtained a favorable binding ruling now faces possible penalties because CBP says the ruling was based on facts the importer misrepresented. Does reliance on that ruling still generally protect the importer from those penalties in this situation?

options.A: Reliance protection generally does not extend to rulings based on misrepresented facts
options.B: CBP bears sole responsibility for verifying the facts, relieving the importer of any duty to check them
options.C: The importer remains fully protected by the ruling despite any misrepresentation made
options.D: Misrepresented facts affect only future rulings and not the ruling that was already issued

question: A broker is classifying imported bathroom fixtures where a section note excludes items designed exclusively for laboratory use, directing such items to a different chapter regardless of their material composition. What must the broker confirm before applying the general fixtures heading?

options.A: Whether the fixture was imported by air freight or by ocean freight into the port
options.B: Whether the fixture is designed exclusively for laboratory use, triggering the exclusion
options.C: Whether the country of origin of the fixture qualifies for a trade preference program, since the program turns on where the goods were made
options.D: Whether the importer has previously filed a protest on a similar bathroom fixture

question: In Savannah, an importer's customs broker is reviewing an entry where the importer claims preferential tariff treatment under a special program administered through temporary legislative provisions rather than the general HTSUS schedule. Which chapter contains these kinds of temporary modifications?

options.A: Chapter 99, addressing temporary legislation and trade remedy modifications
options.B: Chapter 1 of the schedule, which covers live animals under the general provisions
options.C: Chapter 98, which addresses special classification for American goods returned to the country
options.D: GRI 2(a), which governs incomplete or unfinished articles with the essential character

question: A broker is classifying an imported automotive replacement part and finds a chapter note stating that certain parts suitable for use with multiple types of vehicles are classified under a general parts heading rather than with any single vehicle type. How should the broker apply this note?

options.A: Classify the part with whichever single vehicle type the importer primarily sells to customers
options.B: Ignore the note whenever a more specific single-vehicle heading appears to exist in the chapter
options.C: Classify the multi-purpose part under the general parts heading as the note directs
options.D: Classify the part under Chapter 99 as an article covered by a temporary provision

question: An imported article combines a digital camera and a portable video projector built into one integrated housing, where both functions are roughly equal in commercial importance and neither is clearly secondary. After GRI 3(a) fails, what is the next proper analytical step?

options.A: Move directly to GRI 3(c) without attempting essential character analysis
options.B: Attempt essential character analysis under GRI 3(b) before considering GRI 3(c)
options.C: Classify under whichever heading has historically applied to similar hybrid devices
options.D: Default immediately to GRI 4 as the most akin goods provision

question: A broker wants to determine whether a specific imported fastener qualifies as a part of machinery under a parts provision or should instead be classified under a general heading for articles of base metal. What factor is most relevant to this determination?

options.A: Whether the fastener is a dedicated, identifiable component of the specific machine
options.B: Whether the fastener is more expensive than the other components of the machine it accompanies
options.C: Whether the fastener was manufactured in the same country as the machine it will be used on
options.D: Whether the fastener was shipped in the same container as the machine it belongs to

question: In Norfolk, a licensed customs broker is classifying an entry for a camera retailer where the imported article is a specially designed plastic case molded to fit and protect a particular model of digital camera, sold with the camera as one unit. How is this fitted case treated under the GRIs?

options.A: Classified separately under the general heading for plastic articles of this kind
options.B: Classified with the camera under GRI 5(a) as a specially shaped container
options.C: Classified under GRI 3(c) as a tiebreaker between the two competing headings
options.D: Excluded from the entry altogether as a duty-free accessory item for the camera

question: An importer holds a binding ruling issued under Part 177 and later faces a CBP attempt to assess penalties for the same classification described in that ruling. May the importer still use the ruling defensively in responding to those penalties?

options.A: Binding rulings provide no protection against future penalty actions brought by CBP after the entry, and the ruling plays no part in the penalty case
options.B: Only rulings issued within the prior thirty days offer any protection against a penalty action at the port
options.C: Penalty protection requires a separate certification filed annually with CBP for each imported product line
options.D: A valid ruling accurately relied upon generally provides protection against penalties for that classification

question: In Charleston, an importer's customs broker is preparing a binding ruling request for a textile product and must decide whether to include physical samples along with the written description of the merchandise being classified. What is the general guidance on including samples?

options.A: Samples are not permitted to accompany a ruling request when it is filed with CBP
options.B: A ruling request is automatically invalid if any physical sample is included with the letter
options.C: Samples are often helpful and may be requested by CBP to support accurate classification
options.D: Samples replace the need for any written description of the merchandise in the request, whatever the written submission contains

question: In Baltimore, an importer's customs broker is preparing a response for an importer whose counsel argues that CBP should be bound by an internal, unpublished memo discussing classification of a product line rather than by a formal binding ruling. What is the correct response to this argument?

options.A: Any internal CBP document automatically qualifies as a binding ruling for the importer's product line
options.B: An unpublished internal memo does not carry the binding legal effect of a formal Part 177 ruling
options.C: CBP is legally required to issue a formal ruling whenever an internal memo on the product exists
options.D: Unpublished internal memos are more authoritative than published rulings on the same product

question: In Houston, an importer's customs broker is classifying a beauty gift set for a cosmetics importer, where cosmetic products are packaged together with applicator brushes and a mirror compact and sold as one retail set, with the cosmetics clearly the primary value driver. Which classification result follows?

options.A: Each item in the gift set must be entered and classified under its own separate heading
options.B: The mirror alone determines the classification, since it is a permanent and reusable item
options.C: GRI 5(a) governs the set, since the compact functions as a specially fitted container
options.D: GRI 3(b) classifies the set according to the cosmetics providing essential character

question: A broker is classifying an imported industrial valve and finds that a chapter note excludes valves designed exclusively for use in aircraft, directing them to a different chapter covering aircraft parts. What must the broker confirm before applying the general valve heading?

options.A: Whether the retail price of the valve exceeds a specific dollar threshold set by CBP, before the heading can be applied
options.B: Whether the valve was manufactured domestically or brought in from a foreign supplier
options.C: Whether the valve is designed exclusively for aircraft use, triggering the exclusion note
options.D: Whether the importer has previously imported similar valves from the same supplier

question: A shipment of decorative candles is packaged with a matching glass holder, both items clearly intended to function together and marketed as a single home decor product. The candle provides the primary function; the holder is secondary. What controls under GRI 3(b)?

options.A: Whichever item was listed first on the commercial invoice submitted with the entry
options.B: The candle, since it supplies the essential character of the combined product
options.C: The glass holder, since glass is a more durable material than the wax of the candle
options.D: Both items must be classified together under a single residual decor heading

question: In Houston, a trade compliance analyst is classifying goods for a manufacturer and finds an Explanatory Note to a heading suggesting an interpretation that appears to conflict with the plain text of a binding Section Note in the HTSUS. Which source should control classification?

options.A: The binding Section Note, since Explanatory Notes are persuasive but not binding
options.B: The Explanatory Note, since it is issued by the World Customs Organization
options.C: Whichever source the importer's counsel prefers to cite
options.D: Neither source applies once a conflict exists, requiring automatic residual classification

question: In Charleston, a licensed customs broker is advising an importer on an entry where an existing binding ruling on a similar product was issued several years ago, and CBP has since modified its classification position through a later published ruling. What should the broker do?

options.A: Request that CBP reissue the older ruling exactly as it was originally written
options.B: Continue relying on the older ruling, since CBP has not formally revoked it
options.C: Disregard both rulings and classify the goods solely from the Explanatory Notes instead
options.D: Follow the more recent published ruling, since CBP positions can be modified over time

question: In Baltimore, a trade compliance analyst is classifying a shipment for a toy importer where a children's toy playset includes a plastic action figure, a small vehicle, and an accessory base, all packaged and marketed as one coordinated play set. Which GRI most directly governs this shipment?

options.A: GRI 2(a), treating the vehicle as an unfinished version of the figure
options.B: GRI 3(b), since the items together meet a particular need as a retail set
options.C: GRI 5(b), treating the accessory base as ordinary packing material
options.D: Separate classification of each item under its own heading whatever the packaging

question: In Savannah, a licensed customs broker is reviewing the classification of a hand tool for a hardware importer and finds that the item classifies under a heading describing pliers rather than a broader general hardware heading, even though the broader heading also covers the item. Which principle explains this outcome?

options.A: The more specific description in a heading is preferred over a more general one
options.B: The broader heading controls when two headings overlap
options.C: Duty rate differences alone determine which of two overlapping headings applies
options.D: The Explanatory Notes require selecting whichever heading is listed first numerically

question: In Long Beach, a licensed customs broker is classifying a chemical mixture for an industrial importer and finds that the entry describes an article combining two substances, neither of which alone would be classified in the heading claimed for the mixture. What GRI concept most directly governs classifying this kind of combination?

options.A: GRI 5(a), treating the mixture as goods packaged within a specially fitted container for sale
options.B: GRI 1, since a mixture of this kind is named directly by a specific heading
options.C: GRI 6, comparing the competing subheadings before any heading has been determined for the goods
options.D: GRI 2(b), extending relevant headings to mixtures and combinations of materials

question: In Miami, a customs broker is advising an importer of industrial machinery who holds a favorable binding ruling and now asks whether CBP can later change its classification position on that ruling, which the importer has relied on for some time. What is generally true about ruling modification?

options.A: Rulings automatically expire and must be resubmitted to CBP every calendar year for renewal
options.B: A binding ruling cannot be modified once it has been issued, whatever the circumstances
options.C: CBP may modify or revoke a ruling, generally with prospective effect and required notice
options.D: Only the importer may initiate modification of an existing binding ruling, not the agency itself

question: In Baltimore, a customs broker is advising an importer who wonders whether goods missing one inexpensive, easily replaced component still qualify as the finished article under GRI 2(a), given how small the missing piece is. What is the correct legal test?

options.A: Whether the imported goods have the essential character of the complete article
options.B: Whether the importer intends to complete the article within thirty days after the entry is filed
options.C: Whether the value of the missing component exceeds five percent of the total entered value of the goods
options.D: Whether the missing component is separately classifiable under its own heading in the tariff schedule

question: In Houston, a customs compliance manager is classifying eyewear for an optical goods importer and must decide whether the heading naming eyeglass frames specifically or a broader heading for optical goods generally should be applied first. What classification hierarchy resolves this?

options.A: The broader optical goods heading controls, however specific the other description is
options.B: The importer chooses whichever heading yields a lower entered value for the eyewear shipment
options.C: GRI 3(a) prefers the more specific eyeglass frames description over the general heading
options.D: Classification defaults to GRI 4 whenever two headings appear to overlap on their face

question: In Miami, a customs compliance manager is classifying goods for an industrial importer and finds a section note stating that a category of articles classifies in a particular chapter regardless of the material from which they are made. How should the broker treat this note relative to material-based headings elsewhere?

options.A: Material composition takes precedence over a conflicting section note
options.B: The note controls and overrides classification by material composition
options.C: The broker may choose whichever result is more favorable
options.D: The note applies only if the importer requests it in writing

question: In Savannah, a trade compliance analyst is classifying a shipment for a consumer goods importer where two headings, one general and one specific by name and function, both seem to describe the same article, and no Section or Chapter Note resolves the conflict. Which GRI supplies the tiebreaker principle here?

options.A: GRI 4, classifying the goods under the heading for the article they are most akin to
options.B: GRI 2(b), which governs mixtures and combinations of two or more materials
options.C: GRI 3(a), favoring the heading providing the more specific description
options.D: GRI 5(b), which addresses normal packing materials and containers sold with goods

question: In Charleston, a customs compliance manager is reviewing an entry where the commercial invoice describes the merchandise only as general purpose hardware, and the correct heading cannot be determined from that description alone. What is the broker's proper first step?

options.A: Select the heading that carries the lowest applicable duty rate for hardware of this kind
options.B: Obtain sufficiently detailed technical information about composition and function
options.C: Classify under the residual basket provision without any further inquiry into the composition of the goods
options.D: Rely exclusively on the description in the commercial invoice as sufficient for classification

question: In Houston, a customs broker is handling an entry for a power tool that arrived disassembled and is missing only a plastic housing cover that does not affect how the tool works once assembled. Under GRI 2(a), how should this incomplete article be classified?

options.A: As the finished power tool, since it has the complete article's essential character
options.B: As scrap metal pending further manufacture, since the tool is not complete when it arrives
options.C: Under the residual provision for goods not elsewhere specified, because the article is incomplete
options.D: As unassembled parts, with each component classified separately under its own heading

question: In Long Beach, a customs broker is handling an entry for US-made industrial equipment exported for repair abroad and now reimported without having been advanced in value beyond that repair, and the importer asks about special treatment. Which part of the schedule may provide special treatment?

options.A: Chapter 99, which is reserved for temporary trade remedy actions and safeguard measures
options.B: GRI 2(a), which governs incomplete or unfinished articles that have the essential character of the whole
options.C: Chapter 98, addressing special classification including repaired or altered US goods
options.D: GRI 4, which classifies goods according to the most akin article when no other rule applies

question: A first aid kit similar to an earlier example, this time marketed specifically for automotive emergency use and containing a reflective warning triangle, jumper cables, and basic bandages, is packaged together in one bag sold as a single roadside emergency kit. How should the essential character of this particular set most likely be assessed given its stated automotive emergency purpose?

options.A: By evaluating which component most predominates by value, bulk, and role in fulfilling the kit's stated core roadside emergency purpose, which given the marketed purpose could reasonably center on the higher-value jumper cables or warning triangle rather than the bandages
options.B: By selecting the bandages, because medical items control the character of a roadside kit, whatever its stated purpose or the other contents, and the whole kit is entered under the heading that covers the bandages alone in the classification analysis
options.C: By the bag alone, since it physically holds everything and gives the kit its shape, so the container supplies the character of the article for duty, and the contents are treated as packing that follows the bag, and the tools and warning triangle are disregarded when the bag is classified
options.D: By whichever item has the brightest color, since the most visible component in a roadside kit catches the eye of the driver and defines the article for the buyer at the time of entry of the kit into the country

question: In Houston, a customs compliance manager is studying the tariff schedule for a textile importer and observes that subheadings within one heading are divided using colons and indentation, grouping several six-digit provisions beneath one another. When comparing competing subheadings under GRI 6, what principle applies?

options.A: Subheading comparison is prohibited once the correct heading has been chosen for the goods
options.B: Any subheading in the chapter may be compared directly, whatever level it occupies
options.C: The importer selects whichever subheading offers the most favorable duty rate on the entry
options.D: Only subheadings at the same indentation level may be compared to one another

question: In Savannah, a customs broker is reviewing a stainless steel kitchen sink imported packaged together with a matching wire dish rack and sold as one retail unit, and no single heading names the combination. Which GRI governs classifying this retail set?

options.A: GRI 1, applying the heading that names sinks specifically to the whole retail unit
options.B: GRI 3(b), classifying the set by the component giving essential character
options.C: GRI 5, treating the retail packaging that holds the pair as the controlling element
options.D: GRI 2(a), treating the set as an unfinished sink that will be completed by the buyer

question: In Savannah, a customs compliance manager is classifying decorative glass ornaments for a giftware importer, and the goods fit no specifically named heading but fall generally within a chapter covering miscellaneous glass articles. What kind of heading resolves this classification?

options.A: An eo nomine provision naming the glass ornaments by their exact common name in the heading
options.B: A use provision requiring proof of the actual principal use of the ornaments by the importer
options.C: A Chapter 98 provision for goods that were previously exported from the United States and returned
options.D: A basket provision capturing articles not more specifically described elsewhere

question: A rubber boot similar to an earlier example is molded as one continuous piece with a slightly different sole tread pattern than most standard boots, still made entirely of rubber with no other material components. A specific rubber footwear heading and a general rubber articles heading could both potentially apply. Which heading controls, and under which GRI?

options.A: The specific rubber footwear heading controls under GRI 3(a), which prefers the more specific description over the general rubber articles provision
options.B: The general rubber articles heading controls over any more specific alternative, since broader provisions are applied first for simplicity
options.C: GRI 5(b) resolves the matter by treating the sole tread as packing material, since the molded tread protects the boot during shipment
options.D: Neither heading applies to the boot, so the goods cannot be classified under the current schedule and a new ruling is required

question: A denim gift set for toddlers, similar to an earlier infant example, includes matching jeans, a denim vest, and a small fabric sun hat, all in coordinating patterns, packaged together and sold as one retail toddler outfit set. Why would this combination likely qualify as a set under GRI 3(b) rather than requiring separate GRI 1 classification of each piece?

options.A: Because all three items share the identical denim fabric weight measured in ounces per square yard, which ties them together as one outfit for the child at retail, and the outfit is entered under one heading as a single article
options.B: Because the items are classifiable under different headings, are put together to meet the specific need of dressing a toddler for outdoor wear, and are packaged for retail sale without repacking
options.C: Because the items were sewn using the same brand of thread and the same stitching pattern, which shows they were made as one outfit for the toddler, and the thread alone ties the pieces together
options.D: Because each item costs exactly the same wholesale price from the supplier, which shows that no single piece dominates the retail set, so the group is entered together

question: In Baltimore, a customs broker is reviewing a leather goods shipment in which a wallet is packaged inside a branded cardboard gift box made specifically to hold it and sold together with it at retail. How should the gift box be classified?

options.A: Separately under its own heading for paperboard articles
options.B: As a set under GRI 3(b) requiring essential character analysis
options.C: With the wallet under GRI 5(b) as normal packing material
options.D: Excluded from entry as duty-free promotional material

question: CBP Headquarters, after reviewing new technical information about a chemical compound's actual composition, proposes to revoke a previously issued New York ruling that had classified the compound under an incorrect heading, following the required notice and comment procedures. What is the practical effect of a properly completed revocation on future entries of that same compound?

options.A: Going forward, entries of the compound must generally be classified according to the newly established, corrected classification as of the specified effective date
options.B: Nothing changes for the importer, since revocations under this process are purely symbolic and carry no operative effect on future entries of the compound
options.C: Importers may continue using the original New York ruling classification permanently, since a revoked letter keeps its force for the party that requested it
options.D: The revocation applies only to the specific shipment that prompted CBP's initial review at the port, and no other shipments of the compound are affected by it

question: In Long Beach, a customs broker is classifying wooden picture frames imported empty for a frame shop, with no glass or backing included, and the heading names the article directly by its identity rather than describing any function it serves. What kind of provision is this?

options.A: A use provision classified by actual principal use
options.B: A basket provision for articles not elsewhere specified
options.C: An eo nomine provision naming the article by its specific name
options.D: A composite goods provision requiring essential character analysis

question: A classification analyst reviewing the tariff schedule notices that certain Chapter Notes expressly exclude specific articles from the chapter's coverage and direct them instead to a different chapter entirely. What legal weight do such exclusionary Chapter Notes carry when a classifier applies GRI 1?

options.A: Chapter Notes are merely suggestions and can be disregarded if the heading text alone seems to cover the article, since a broker may rely on the plain words of the schedule in the printed book, and CBP reviews only the entry summary, so the notes may be passed over whenever a heading looks close enough
options.B: Chapter Notes are relevant only for statistical reporting and do not affect the legal classification of the goods, since the heading text carries legal force at entry
options.C: Chapter Notes apply only to the importer who specifically requested a binding ruling, since other entries are classified on the heading language alone and without the notes, and the ruling letter governs that importer only, and no chapter note obliges the importer to look any further than the heading it chose
options.D: Chapter Notes carry binding legal force under GRI 1 and must be applied alongside the heading text, meaning an article expressly excluded by a Chapter Note cannot be classified in that chapter regardless of how closely the heading text might otherwise seem to describe it

question: A tractor part similar to an earlier example, this time a seat cushion assembly designed and shaped to fit only one specific tractor model's seat frame, with no application to any other equipment, is imported separately from the tractor. How does the general parts rule direct classification of this dedicated cushion assembly?

options.A: Under Chapter 99 exclusively, bypassing any parts classification analysis, since tractor components are covered by temporary trade measures on machinery at entry
options.B: As a generic upholstered seating article under a general furniture heading, ignoring its dedicated tractor-specific design, since the cushion resembles ordinary seating in appearance
options.C: As a part suitable for use solely or principally with that particular tractor model, classified accordingly under the relevant parts provision rather than a general seating heading
options.D: Under GRI 5(a), which treats the cushion assembly as a fitted case for the tractor seat frame because it is shaped to that frame alone, so the case rule governs the entry, so the duty rate follows the fitted case treatment

question: A shipment of imported furniture becomes subject to an additional antidumping duty order specific to that product category from a particular country, on top of its regular classification under a furniture heading in Chapters 1 through 97. How does this additional duty typically interact with the underlying HTSUS classification analysis?

options.A: The antidumping duty is applied in addition to, and separately administered from, the underlying GRI-based classification, rather than altering the base heading itself
options.B: Antidumping duties can be applied only to raw materials and not to finished furniture, so the order cannot reach an assembled article like this one
options.C: The General Rules of Interpretation cease to apply once an antidumping order affects a product category, so the goods are classified by the order rather than the schedule
options.D: The antidumping order automatically reclassifies the furniture into a different chapter, so the base heading changes when the order is published

question: A specialized valve, machined and dimensioned to fit only one particular model of industrial compressor and unusable in any other equipment due to its unique thread pattern, is imported separately from the compressor. How does the general parts rule typically govern the classification of this valve?

options.A: As a generic article of steel under a residual basket provision, disregarding its dedicated compressor-specific design and the thread pattern that limits its use
options.B: As a part suitable for use solely or principally with that particular compressor, classified accordingly under the relevant parts provision
options.C: Under GRI 5(a), which treats the valve as a fitted case presented with the compressor because it is shaped to its thread pattern
options.D: Under whichever heading the compressor manufacturer's marketing brochure suggests, since the maker's literature shows the intended use of the valve

question: A generator part, specifically an alternator bracket machined to fit only one manufacturer's specific generator model, is imported separately from the generator itself, with no interchangeability with any other equipment due to its unique mounting configuration. How does the general parts rule typically direct classification of this bracket?

options.A: Under GRI 5(a), which treats the alternator bracket as a fitted case for the generator because it is shaped to mount on that model, so the case rule governs the entry
options.B: As scrap metal, since a bracket that cannot be used on any other machine has no dedicated tariff status and must be entered as waste
options.C: Under Chapter 99 exclusively, bypassing any parts classification analysis, since generator components are covered by temporary trade measures on machinery, and no parts provision needs to be examined for the item
options.D: As a part suitable for use solely or principally with that particular generator, classified accordingly under the relevant parts provision rather than a generic metal articles heading

question: An unassembled wardrobe closet arrives in one shipment containing pre-finished wooden side panels, doors, a top and base panel, and all connecting hardware, from a single manufacturer for a single retail buyer, requiring only routine assembly. The panels already display the finished wardrobe's exact shape and proportions. What does GRI 2(a) direct for classifying this shipment?

options.A: No classification is possible until the wardrobe is physically assembled after importation, since the schedule has no heading for loose panels shipped together in one container
options.B: Classification of the hardware bag alone as controlling for the entire shipment, since the connecting parts are what turn the panels into a wardrobe for tariff purposes
options.C: Classification as the complete, assembled wardrobe closet under the finished furniture heading, since the components already possess the essential character of the finished article
options.D: Classification as raw lumber under Chapter 44, disregarding the shaping already performed on the panels and doors because the unit is not assembled at the port, so the panels are entered as separate pieces of lumber

question: A broker prepares an entry for a wooden bookcase that arrives fully assembled, and the merchandise could arguably fall under both a heading specifically naming bookcases and a broader heading covering wooden furniture generally. Applying GRI 1 and then GRI 3(a) together, which heading actually controls, and why?

options.A: The classifier may choose either heading freely based on which one offers the lower duty rate, since cost is the practical result the importer wants from the entry, and both headings describe the bookcase
options.B: The heading specifically naming bookcases, because GRI 3(a) prefers the more specific description over a general one once GRI 1 alone does not resolve the choice between two candidate headings
options.C: Neither heading applies to the assembled bookcase, and a residual chapter must be used instead because the goods are not fully described by either heading, so the entry is held for review
options.D: The broader wooden furniture heading controls, because general provisions take precedence over specific ones for administrative simplicity at the port of entry, and brokers may pick the general rule

question: An importer receives a New York ruling classifying imported ceramic tableware under a particular heading. A competing importer of nearly identical tableware later requests a separate ruling on their own similar product and receives a different classification from CBP. What does this situation typically indicate under the ruling system?

options.A: Differing rulings may reflect genuine factual differences between the two products, or may indicate that one ruling requires further review by Headquarters to ensure consistency across similar merchandise
options.B: Rulings do not differ for similar merchandise, so one of the two letters must have been issued in error by the office that wrote it, and CBP must withdraw both
options.C: The first ruling automatically controls the classification, and the second is void immediately upon issuance, since the earlier letter takes precedence over the later one for all importers
options.D: Both rulings are automatically nullified whenever any inconsistency between them arises, and the importer must start the ruling process over from the beginning with a new request letter, and both earlier letters lose their force at the ports

question: A heading reads 'hammers and sledge hammers, with heads of iron or steel' naming the article specifically by type and material rather than by its use. An importer brings in decorative novelty hammers sold purely as paperweights rather than for any striking function. How would this eo nomine-style heading generally treat the novelty hammers?

options.A: They require a full principal use analysis under Additional US Rule of Interpretation 1(a) before classification is possible, since the goods are sold as decorative articles rather than tools
options.B: They would be excluded from the heading because their actual use is decorative rather than functional striking, so the paperweights fall outside the hammer provision
options.C: Because the heading names the article by type and material without use-limiting language, it generally covers the article regardless of a particular individual unit's actual intended use
options.D: They must be classified under an unrelated novelty items chapter, since the importer's stated use governs the entry, not the heading language about the article's shape

question: A retail set contains a men's leather belt, matching leather wallet, and a small leather keychain, all packaged together in one box for sale as a single coordinated accessories gift set. Which three conditions must be satisfied for this combination to qualify as a set under the recognized GRI 3(b) test?

options.A: Each item in the box must independently weigh more than a minimum threshold set by CBP for accessory sets at retail sale, and the total weight fixes the duty rate
options.B: All items must share an identical shade of leather dye and finish, so the set looks uniform when it is displayed in the store, and the dye batch must match
options.C: All items must have been tanned at the same tannery, since a common origin is what ties the pieces together as one article for duty purposes, so the test is satisfied on that point
options.D: Classifiable under different headings, put up together to meet a specific need or carry out a specific activity, and packaged for retail sale without repacking

question: An importer brings in a finished stainless steel serving tray with no other article attached and no accompanying components. A single heading in Chapter 73 describes household articles of stainless steel. Under GRI 1, what is the first analytical step the classifier must take?

options.A: Examine the terms of the heading and any relevant Section and Chapter Notes to see whether they fully describe the tray
options.B: Skip directly to the GRI 6 subheading comparisons, since the heading already names the article and only the digits differ
options.C: Determine the duty rate first and then work backward to the heading that produces the lowest duty for the tray at entry
options.D: Apply GRI 4 by analogy before considering any heading text, since the tray has no exact match in the schedule for trays

question: An importer submits a written request under 19 CFR Part 177 asking CBP to classify a proposed new line of imported furniture, including drawings, material specifications, and a physical sample, before any purchase order has been placed with the foreign manufacturer. What must generally be true about the transaction described for CBP to accept and rule on this request?

options.A: CBP will rule only on transactions that are already the subject of pending litigation, since the court record supplies the facts needed for a ruling, and no other source of facts is needed
options.B: The transaction must involve merchandise not yet imported, described with sufficient specificity for CBP to reach a definitive classification determination
options.C: The request must omit any physical sample or technical specification, since CBP rules only on the written description of the goods supplied in the letter
options.D: The furniture must already have been imported and entered before the request is filed, since a ruling is a review of an entry that has already been made

question: A first aid kit sold at retail contains adhesive bandages, antiseptic wipes, a small pair of scissors, and gauze pads, all packaged together in a single zippered pouch marketed for household emergency use. The classifier confirms this meets the GRI 3(b) set criteria. How should the essential character of this particular set most likely be assessed?

options.A: By evaluating which component most predominates by value, bulk, and its role in fulfilling the kit's core first aid purpose, which for many such kits centers on the wound-care items rather than the pouch itself
options.B: By the pouch alone, since it physically holds everything together and gives the kit its shape, so the container supplies the character of the whole article for classification, and the contents are treated as packing that follows the bag
options.C: By whichever item was manufactured most recently before the kit was assembled, since the newest component sets the character of the assembled article for duty purposes, and the other components are ignored in the analysis
options.D: By selecting the item with the shortest shelf life, since the component that expires first governs how the kit is used and therefore its character as a set under the GRI 3(b) rules

question: A gift set includes a fountain pen, a leather-bound journal, and a small bottle of ink, packaged together for retail sale as a single writing-themed gift item. After applying GRI 3(a) and 3(b), the classifier finds that no single component clearly predominates in value, bulk, or function relative to the set's overall writing purpose. What rule resolves the classification next?

options.A: GRI 1 alone, disregarding the set analysis and reading only the terms of the heading
options.B: GRI 3(c), classifying under whichever qualifying heading occurs last in numerical order
options.C: GRI 5(b), treating the leather journal as packing material for the pen and ink in the box
options.D: GRI 4, classifying the set by analogy to an unrelated article with a similar writing purpose

question: A brake caliper is manufactured and machined so that it is suitable for use solely with a particular model of motorcycle and cannot be adapted for use on any other vehicle due to its unique mounting geometry. It is imported separately from the motorcycle itself. How does the general parts rule typically direct classification of such a dedicated component?

options.A: As a generic article of iron or steel under a residual basket provision, since the caliper is a metal article before it is a part of anything, for the entry
options.B: Under GRI 5(b) as packing material, since the caliper is boxed with the motorcycle and protects the brake assembly in transit to the dealer, and no parts provision needs to be consulted for the entry
options.C: Under whichever heading the freight forwarder selects on the bill of lading, since the transport document governs the classification used at the port of entry
options.D: As a part of the motorcycle under the relevant parts provision, since it is identifiable as suitable for use solely or principally with that particular vehicle

question: A customs broker is advising a client on the general reliability of a published CBP ruling letter that closely matches the client's planned import of a novel consumer product. The broker explains the basic legal framework governing such rulings under 19 CFR Part 177. Which statement best summarizes that framework?

options.A: Rulings are purely advisory opinions with no binding legal effect on CBP, so an importer may rely on them only as informal guidance about the heading for the goods, and the port may classify differently at any time
options.B: A properly issued binding ruling reflects CBP's official classification position for the described merchandise and facts, generally reliable unless and until properly modified or revoked through required procedures
options.C: Rulings expire automatically after thirty days, whatever action CBP has taken, and the importer must file a new request each quarter of the year for its entries
options.D: Rulings apply only to entries made at the specific port where the ruling request was filed, so a broker importing at another port must obtain a separate letter for the same goods, even when the facts are identical

question: CBP Headquarters issues a Headquarters ruling letter that expressly modifies and supersedes a previously issued New York ruling on the classification of imported footwear, following required notice and comment procedures. What is the effect on importers who had been relying on the original New York ruling for identical merchandise?

options.A: Going forward, importers must generally follow the new Headquarters classification for entries after the effective date specified, though prior good-faith reliance before that date is typically treated differently under applicable procedures
options.B: The New York ruling automatically becomes binding on Headquarters instead, so the older classification continues to govern until the importer agrees to the change proposed in the notice, which the importer may simply decline to accept
options.C: Importers may simply ignore the Headquarters ruling and continue using the original classification indefinitely, since a ruling issued in New York is the highest authority a broker may rely on for entries at any port in the country
options.D: Nothing changes for any importer, since Headquarters rulings do not affect a New York ruling that was issued earlier, and each letter stands on its own as binding advice

question: A cashmere and silk blended scarf, containing 70 percent cashmere and 30 percent silk fibers woven together into one fabric, arrives with no single heading naming this precise blend by name. How does the tariff schedule generally direct classification of such a mixed-fiber textile article?

options.A: GRI 5(a), which treats the cashmere and silk blend as a fitted case for the scarf it forms when presented for sale, so the case rule rather than the fiber rules governs the entry
options.B: GRI 1 alone resolves the classification without regard to fiber content, since the heading for scarves covers the article whatever it is made of in the blend at entry
options.C: GRI 2(b) extends the relevant fiber-based headings to mixtures, with further resolution under GRI 3 if more than one heading remains applicable after that extension
options.D: GRI 4, classifying the scarf by analogy to the most similar woven article without considering the fiber percentages in the blend, even though the fibers were woven together

question: A batch of spices is imported consisting of a proprietary blend of ground cumin, paprika, and garlic powder mixed together before importation, rather than shipped as three separate, unmixed spices. No single heading names this exact proprietary blend by name. How does GRI 2(b) address this situation?

options.A: GRI 2(b) extends any heading referring to a material or substance, such as a named spice, to include mixtures or combinations of that substance with other materials, requiring further analysis under GRI 3 if more than one heading could then apply
options.B: GRI 5(b) treats the blended spices as packing material for the individual spices, since the mixture merely holds the separate ingredients together in one retail container for the buyer, so the packing rule rather than the mixture rule controls the entry
options.C: The blend cannot be classified under the HTSUS, since no heading names the exact combination of cumin, paprika, and garlic powder mixed together, so the spices cannot be entered
options.D: The blend is automatically classified under whichever spice was added in the largest single measured quantity at the moment of mixing, without further rule application or any consideration of the headings that name the individual spices

question: A plastic action figure is imported with its head, torso, and legs already molded and attached, missing only its small plastic accessory weapon, which will be added after importation from separately sourced components. The figure already displays the complete recognizable form of the finished toy character. Which GRI addresses classifying this figure as though it were the complete toy?

options.A: GRI 3(c), the numerical tie-breaker rule applied to the competing toy headings
options.B: GRI 5(b), which covers packing materials and containers presented with the goods they hold
options.C: GRI 2(a), unfinished articles having the essential character of the complete article
options.D: GRI 6, which compares only the subheadings beneath a single heading at the same level

question: A domestic manufacturer petitions for antidumping duties on a particular imported steel product, and after investigation an antidumping duty order is issued requiring additional duties on top of the product's regular Chapter 72 classification. Where in the HTSUS structure would a classifier expect the mechanism for applying such additional antidumping duties to be reflected?

options.A: The base classification in Chapter 72 is permanently altered to a new heading solely because of the antidumping order, so the goods enter under a different tariff number for as long as the order remains in force
options.B: Antidumping duties have no relationship to the tariff schedule, since they are collected by the Department of Commerce outside the classification system used by CBP, and no tariff number reflects them
options.C: Antidumping duties replace the General Rules of Interpretation for that product, so the base heading is chosen without reference to the schedule, and CBP does not reclassify the merchandise
options.D: Antidumping duties are applied through Chapter 99 and related administrative mechanisms alongside the underlying Chapter 1 through 97 classification, rather than by changing the base classification itself

question: A football, fully stitched and shaped with all panels attached but not yet inflated, is imported in this partially completed state, with inflation to occur domestically before retail sale. The ball already has the complete recognizable shape, panel construction, and essential character of a finished football. Under GRI 2(a), how is the uninflated ball treated?

options.A: Under Chapter 98 as an article returned to the United States, since the ball was made here and is coming back after export for finishing
options.B: As raw rubber material only, since the ball has not been inflated and cannot be used as a ball until the air is added at the plant
options.C: As an unfinished article having the essential character of the complete football, classified under the heading for finished footballs
options.D: Under GRI 5(a) as a fitted case, since the stitched panels form a covering that holds the air once the ball is fully inflated for play

question: CBP's National Commodity Specialist Division issues a New York ruling classifying an imported toy under a specific toy heading. Two years later, CBP Headquarters determines, after reviewing new information about the toy's actual play function, that the original classification was incorrect and proposes to modify it. What must Headquarters generally do before the modification becomes legally effective?

options.A: Nothing, since HQ modifications take effect the moment they are drafted internally and are applied to entries right away, and no publication of the change is needed
options.B: Publish the proposed modification for public notice and comment as generally required before a final modification takes effect
options.C: Wait for a federal court order before modifying any ruling, since only a judge may set aside a published classification decision
options.D: Obtain the personal written consent of the original importer before any modification of the ruling can occur at the port

question: Industrial machinery originally manufactured in the United States and exported for use at a foreign facility is later brought back into the United States in exactly the same condition, with no repairs, alterations, or advancement in value having occurred while abroad. What Chapter 98 subheading is specifically designed for this precise fact pattern?

options.A: The Chapter 99 temporary safeguard provisions, since the machinery is coming back into the country after a period of foreign use, and safeguard duties apply to returned machinery under a trade action
options.B: The repairs and alterations subheading, since machinery used abroad is inherently subject to wear and tear that changes its value before it comes back into the United States again
options.C: The subheading covering products of the United States exported and returned without advancement in value or improvement in condition, commonly referred to as American goods returned
options.D: The eo nomine provision naming industrial machinery generally, since the article is machinery before it is a returned good and the heading describes it by name, so no Chapter 98 analysis is needed on the entry

question: An unassembled kitchen cabinet arrives in one shipment containing pre-cut wooden panels, hinges, handles, and all necessary screws, from one supplier for one buyer, needing only routine simple-tool assembly to become a complete cabinet. The panels already display the shape and proportions of the finished cabinet's sides, top, and doors. Under GRI 2(a), what is the classification outcome?

options.A: The panels must be classified separately as raw lumber under Chapter 44, since the cabinet is not assembled when it arrives at the port of entry for the buyer
options.B: The shipment is classified as the complete, assembled cabinet under the finished cabinet heading, since it already has the essential character of the assembled article
options.C: The screws alone determine the classification for the whole shipment, since the fasteners are what make the parts into a single article at entry at the port
options.D: GRI 2(a) does not apply to furniture components, so unassembled cabinets are entered as separate wooden parts under their own headings in Chapter 44, so the completed article rule cannot be applied to them

question: A denim jean set marketed for infants includes matching jeans, a denim jacket, and a soft cotton bib, all in coordinating patterns, packaged together and sold as one retail baby gift set. Applying the GRI 3(b) set test, why would this combination likely qualify as a set rather than requiring GRI 1 classification of each piece separately?

options.A: Because all three items are the same color and pattern, so they are sold as one article rather than three separate pieces of clothing for the infant at retail, and the group is entered under a single tariff number for the outfit
options.B: Because all three items were manufactured by the same factory and shipped together in one carton, they are treated as one article under the set rule at the time of importation
options.C: Because the items are classifiable under different headings, are put together to meet the specific need of dressing and caring for an infant, and are packaged for retail sale without repacking
options.D: Because the price of each individual item in the gift set is identical, the pieces have no single dominant component and are treated as a set under the GRI 3(b) rule for retail sets

question: A wooden bookcase is imported fully assembled, with a heading available that names bookcases specifically and a broader heading covering wooden furniture generally. The classifier applies GRI 1 first, then must resolve any apparent conflict between the two candidate headings. What result follows?

options.A: GRI 5(a) resolves the matter by treating the bookcase as a fitted case for the books that will be placed on its shelves
options.B: The general heading for wooden furniture controls over any more specific heading, since the broader provision covers the full range of goods made of wood
options.C: Nothing can be determined about the classification without first obtaining a binding ruling from CBP for the specific bookcase
options.D: GRI 3(a) directs classification under the heading specifically naming bookcases, since it provides the more specific description

question: A wristwatch with a leather band arrives with the case fully assembled but the movement not yet installed, since the movement will be added after importation at a separate facility. The imported article already presents the recognizable form, dial opening, and case shape of a finished watch. Under GRI 2(a), how is this treated?

options.A: As an unfinished article having the essential character of the complete watch, classified under the heading for finished watches
options.B: As raw material only, since the movement is missing and the case cannot tell time without it, so the article has no essential character
options.C: Under Chapter 98 as American goods returned, if the watch case was made in the United States and is coming back after an export for finishing
options.D: Under a residual basket provision because it is incomplete, since no heading names a watch without a movement installed inside the case

question: An importer of solar panels learns that an additional safeguard duty applies to certain imported solar cells under a temporary trade action, on top of the panels' regular classification under their photovoltaic device heading in Chapters 1 through 97. Where would a classifier expect to find the additional safeguard duty rate itself listed?

options.A: Nowhere in the schedule, since safeguard duties are imposed by presidential proclamation and are collected outside the printed tariff schedule at entry
options.B: In the General Notes that precede Chapter 1, where safeguard measures on solar products are listed for all importers to check before filing the entry
options.C: Within Chapter 99, which sets out temporary duty modifications such as safeguard measures applied in addition to the underlying merchandise classification
options.D: Under the alphabetical index only, where the additional duty on solar cells is listed beside the ordinary rate for the goods by product name, and no heading in the schedule needs to be consulted

question: A hair clip made of two different materials, a metal spring mechanism and a decorative plastic shell, is imported as one finished accessory item. Neither material component is separately packaged, and the article is a single physical object rather than a set of distinct articles. How should this article be classified?

options.A: As a composite good under GRI 3(b), classified according to whichever material or component gives the article its essential character
options.B: As a set under the three-part GRI 3(b) test for retail sets, with essential character given to the plastic shell because it is the visible part
options.C: Under GRI 5(b) as packing material, since the plastic shell surrounds and protects the metal spring inside the clip when it is presented for sale
options.D: Under GRI 4 by analogy to the most similar finished accessory, since no heading describes the article by name in the schedule

question: An unfinished golf club head is imported with its basic clubface, hosel, and sole already shaped and forged, lacking only final polishing and the shaft, which will be attached domestically. The head already presents the recognizable form and essential character of a finished golf club head. Under GRI 2(a), how should this be classified?

options.A: As scrap metal, since the head cannot function as a golf club without the shaft attached and has no other use in that condition at the time of entry
options.B: As an unfinished golf club head having the essential character of the finished article, classified accordingly under the heading for golf club heads
options.C: Under the Chapter 99 temporary provisions, since unfinished sporting goods are covered by trade action measures during the period they remain in force
options.D: Under GRI 5(a) as a fitted case, since the club head is shaped to hold the shaft that will be inserted into it after importation at the plant, and the case rule then governs the duty rate

question: A silver necklace is imported alongside matching silver earrings and a silver bracelet, all made of the identical metal and design pattern, packaged together in one presentation box and sold as a single bridal jewelry set at retail. Applying GRI 3(b), how would the essential character of this jewelry set most likely be determined?

options.A: By classifying only the earrings and ignoring the necklace and bracelet, since earrings are the piece that identifies the set as bridal jewelry for the buyer, and the remaining pieces simply follow that choice
options.B: By whichever piece has the greatest surface area, rather than its value or the role it plays when the pieces are worn together, since the largest visible piece controls the character of the set
options.C: Because all three pieces are made of the same material and serve a closely related decorative jewelry purpose, essential character may be difficult to isolate to one piece, potentially requiring GRI 3(c) as a last resort
options.D: By the color and the finish of the presentation box, since the packaging identifies the set and carries the brand's identity to the buyer at retail, and therefore fixes the classification of everything inside, whatever the three pieces are made of

question: A steel bracket is manufactured and shaped so that it is suitable for use solely with a particular model of industrial conveyor machine and has no other practical application. It arrives separately from the conveyor itself. How is such a dedicated part generally classified under the parts provisions?

options.A: As a part of the conveyor machine under the general parts rule for goods suitable for use solely or principally with a particular machine
options.B: Under GRI 5(a), which treats the bracket as a fitted case presented with the conveyor machine, so the case rule governs the entry
